**BlackRock Is the Problem Larry Fink Warns About**
By Will Hild
BlackRock CEO Larry Fink recently **[argued](https://substack.com/redirect/6801f59f-538b-4aa5-a23a-c6ea6a21e05e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** that an Executive Order to **[curb](https://substack.com/redirect/743ff558-b5e3-4dbb-8a7a-df08be671399?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** the influence of large proxy advisers and index funds would empower "foreigners" and "activists." We do need to stop foreign investors and political operatives from interfering with American companies, but the record shows that BlackRock has a long history of empowering such interests, and it remains a major part of the problem. Especially with the order now **[signed](https://substack.com/redirect/93a91b15-d8c1-4d66-ad52-6a377bd952b6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** by President Trump, Mr. Fink should put his words into action and actually stop conduct that he now admits is harmful to American interests.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/13c103c6-961b-4c2e-845f-5a696f70e95f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**[Over](https://substack.com/redirect/8f810e09-9240-4c3d-8de2-c595ae7d1550?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** 40% of BlackRock's assets are foreign-owned. According to a Congressional investigation, **[Norway](https://substack.com/redirect/6b8dc5dc-04a5-4b32-a0d9-d80f85c04003?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and **[Japan](https://substack.com/redirect/0459e292-fed9-4bff-8151-a7e0f5991967?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** 's government pension funds pressured BlackRock into changing its shareholder votes and joining Climate Action 100+. Afterwards, BlackRock's votes for environmental proposals increased _tenfold_(from **[6%](https://substack.com/redirect/fa7805d4-bd39-4deb-b092-4a5e97b8fa2f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to **[64%](https://substack.com/redirect/f00c1dba-3ea3-414e-be8f-6db81c33614f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**), and its votes against directors on climate-related issues increased _fivefold_ (from **[55](https://substack.com/redirect/72099757-dc62-452e-90d3-dfa5c3b76760?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to **[255](https://substack.com/redirect/b3d95f17-d4f5-4245-820b-fc7e366b9427?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**).
Similarly, BlackRock **[became](https://substack.com/redirect/4a3eca7d-f579-42e6-9d5c-20e09be8080f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** one of the first global asset managers to have a wholly owned onshore mutual fund business in China. Even George Soros **[opined](https://substack.com/redirect/ea9497b4-2800-442c-8a98-c79b416bbe9c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** that this move "will damage the national security interests of the U.S." BlackRock has repeatedly voted for traditional energy companies to adopt emissions targets and advocacy approaches that force a transition to wind and solar, such as at **[Chevron](https://substack.com/redirect/7e564db7-b59f-40b7-baed-22cf5c9c6ded?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) , [ConocoPhillips](https://substack.com/redirect/9c750f4b-a383-4dce-9d91-6c4fd90c06b4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**, and **[Berkshire Hathaway](https://substack.com/redirect/549a8621-2507-42b3-9fc6-eff74497710a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).** Since wind and solar supply chains are 80-90% **[dominated](https://substack.com/redirect/1dfb7f95-df7d-4525-807a-d46d33fd8418?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** by China, BlackRock's actions not only harm these American companies but also align with the strategic goals of the United States' greatest adversary. This is not a hypothetical problem--it was recently reported that **[rogue](https://substack.com/redirect/b93a6495-850f-4e9a-9421-3f01eee0d762?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** communication devices were found in Chinese solar power inverters.
BlackRock continues to promote foreign influence on American companies. While SEC Chairman Paul Atkins has threatened to require foreign companies to abandon foreign accounting standards because of their focus on **[immaterial](https://substack.com/redirect/15dcc49e-1830-498d-9510-82438c2210eb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** sustainability requirements, BlackRock **[imposes](https://substack.com/redirect/2d5c7cfc-6117-444b-9ced-9bcaa0339460?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [these](https://substack.com/redirect/3af61a93-7064-4e10-adfc-471ec6ef940e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** same foreign requirements, which the International Sustainability Standards Board marketed as "**[ushering](https://substack.com/redirect/a51cdad5-ef1b-44f9-aeb5-b30472194c59?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in a new era of sustainability-related disclosures," on American firms.
BlackRock also **[maintains membership](https://substack.com/redirect/ae3f6a73-5ade-493c-92ec-b6693799bbbb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in the United Nations Principles for Responsible Investment, whose members **[promise](https://substack.com/redirect/cfea5f37-839c-4a6a-9e73-e7d37c7b03e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to "be active owners and incorporate ESG issues into our ownership policies and practices." In addition, BlackRock's Vice Chairman **[helps lead](https://substack.com/redirect/6579d6cb-7219-4f9f-a3a8-5f97adc8c417?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** the UN-initiated Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero, which organizes asset managers to "**[accelerate](https://substack.com/redirect/6579d6cb-7219-4f9f-a3a8-5f97adc8c417?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** the transition to a net-zero global economy."
[](https://substack.com/redirect/4f649e6f-0480-48c9-9579-d61944c02cfc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
BlackRock continues to use its proxy voting to support environmental activists like the Accountability Board, an organization **[led](https://substack.com/redirect/42cf0819-26e9-4ed2-a77e-4e9877ab2e79?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** by the **[individual](https://substack.com/redirect/d1a1fa97-42e0-48ad-afe0-49eae224599e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** who invented the "holocaust on a plate" ad campaign for PETA. The Accountability Board recently pressured restaurants to cut emissions in line with net-zero targets. Reaching net zero in agriculture **[requires](https://substack.com/redirect/168f911c-f143-4aaa-93a6-d2be12d0a52a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** cutting U.S. beef consumption in half. That goal makes no financial sense for a restaurant that sells beef or hamburgers. Nevertheless, since last year, BlackRock has voted in favor of the Accountability Board's proposals regarding emissions reduction at **[Jack in the Box](https://substack.com/redirect/e912e619-2557-46e4-9670-c20557e534d7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) , [Wingstop](https://substack.com/redirect/658f2817-6b7f-45db-a151-269f395100a3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Denny's](https://substack.com/redirect/2262e019-4ed2-4ed9-9080-1c45e0bdf2c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**, and **[Cracker Barrel](https://substack.com/redirect/08e95101-ef53-4fed-bc2d-59ebc1cd8474?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).** Because BlackRock owns a large share of these companies (almost **[15%](https://substack.com/redirect/01b5a86a-46b8-4797-9e9c-106811a57c66?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in the case of Cracker Barrel), its activism has often been decisive.
These recent votes follow a long history of BlackRock supporting environmental activists. For example, BlackRock voted against the reelection of the chair of **[Transdigm](https://substack.com/redirect/cc1f951e-7a7c-4d95-946b-27e21288ce6e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** for "**[failure](https://substack.com/redirect/5d9807f7-0ccc-422c-a291-2f240c999692?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** "to adopt quantitative greenhouse gas emissions goals." BlackRock also famously supported the **[2021 vote](https://substack.com/redirect/f92db1b6-ed54-4586-b919-ef06e68166f3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to install directors chosen by climate activists onto Exxon's Board.
BlackRock has been equally activist on DEI. Mr. Fink previously stated his philosophy that companies need to "**[force behaviors](https://substack.com/redirect/cb9d1625-98af-493d-bd96-1337689be039?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** " to increase diversity. BlackRock bragged in 2021 that its top reason for voting against directors was that the Board failed to meet diversity quotas. That year, BlackRock voted against **[648](https://substack.com/redirect/9b4f48b5-4d16-4c69-8db3-42370200ad25?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** directors based on diversity, compared to only 246 based on the second-most-frequent reason (compensation). That philosophy remains. BlackRock's current proxy voting guidelines **[state](https://substack.com/redirect/8768c1cb-fb07-4f1b-a7d6-533299b191c5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** that it will vote against board members "to the extent an S&P 500 company board is an outlier" on diversity.
For all these reasons, the Executive Order signed last month is a good start. Given conflicts of interest between large foreign asset owners and American retail investors, preventing BlackRock from voting or engaging with companies is a reasonable solution. BlackRock's potential conflicts are likely to worsen, as the firm could use its low-fee public equity votes to boost the value of its higher-fee private equity offerings.
Mr. Fink correctly recognizes that foreign influence and politically motivated wreckers skew proxy voting from its only legitimate purpose--maximizing risk-adjusted returns for investors. His mistake is ignoring, or failing to stop, BlackRock's substantial role in that problem.

**Hild has been a[longtime opponent of the ESG movement](https://substack.com/redirect/f20df732-9433-4659-9a5a-3a46ddaad773?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and specifically of Larry Fink's role in advancing progressive political objectives through "corporate engagement" with the shares he holds as a fiduciary. Will and Consumers' Research has [mobilized](https://substack.com/redirect/1b2ed562-0555-4069-862a-b18febefbccf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [numerous](https://substack.com/redirect/85d6337f-4b7e-4cd8-b622-3880e6b3f13e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [efforts](https://substack.com/redirect/43b0079d-72dd-4b66-bfa7-d048f5f18d8b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to expose, halt, and roll-back ESG policies pushed by BlackRock and similar firms, [often with considerable success](https://substack.com/redirect/2b7b1122-3478-4695-88a5-cb35961fed32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**

| | Yesterday, on the 5-year anniversary of the January 6 attack on our nation's Capitol, I learned two things that stunned me. **Yesterday morning, as I was preparing to speak on the Senate floor, I learned that the plaque honoring the police officers who heroically defended the U.S. Capitol, members of Congress, and our staff during the January 6, 2021, attack is sitting neglected in a back room.** _This plaque isn't optional._ Congress ordered it to be displayed through a law we passed in 2022. Failing to do so is an egregious insult to every officer who held the line that day, to those who were injured, and to the five officers who died as a result of the attack. That's why I'm working with Senator Thom Tillis of North Carolina on a bipartisan resolution to immediately display the plaque in the Senate wing of the Capitol while we continue pushing for full compliance with the law requiring it to be displayed properly. Then, I saw something else that stopped me cold. **The White House's new January 6 website rewrites history — portraying a violent attack on our democracy as something else entirely, and targeting political opponents with language that is chillingly Orwellian.****_It is disinformation, plain and simple._** This is what we're up against: a deliberate effort to distort the truth, erase accountability, and normalize authoritarianism. I'm ringing the alarm bells because our democracy depends on remembering what happened, honoring courage, and refusing to let lies take hold. **I will not stop fighting to defend the truth, the Constitution, and the people who stood up for our democracy when it mattered most.** Onward, _Jeff_ | Express Donate: If you've stored your info with ActBlue Express, we'll process your contribution to Jeff Merkley instantly:

in the Gulf of Mexico. Further exploitation of our communities, coasts, and
precious waters by Big Oil and Gas would put us all in danger — we must act. We won’t stand by while Trump auctions off our coasts to Big Oil and Gas. Peter ,
The killing of a U.S. citizen by ICE in Minneapolis today is horrifying, tragic, and unacceptable. Our hearts are with the victim’s family, friends, and the community that is once again mourning a life stolen by federally-sanctioned violence.
The right to observe, protest, and speak out against injustice is fundamental in a democracy. When federal agents answer those rights with bullets, it is not only a profound moral failure – it is a threat to the very foundation of our country.
This must be a turning point. ICE must be held accountable, and Kristi Noem’s Department of Homeland Security must answer for its actions
GOTV PAC stands with Minneapolis communities, with protestors exercising their rights, and with all Americans who refuse to accept a country where federal agents kill people in the street.
We urge everyone reading this to contact their members of Congress. Demand an immediate investigation. Demand justice. Demand change.
Lives are at stake.
GOTV PAC

name: Pramila Jayapal
subject: ICE just crossed another red line
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
What ICE is doing in communities across the country is violence.
#
ICE just crossed another horrific red line, Peter.
Today, ICE shot and killed a woman in her car as she was attempting to drive away.
The violence and aggression must stop. And we must get ICE out of our cities.
This is not the first time Trump’s ICE has shot at civilians. And the Trump administration is _already_ pushing a narrative that doesn’t match eyewitness accounts or what video footage has captured.
**What ICE is doing in communities across the country is violence.**
Our communities deserve real protection, dignity, and accountability — not federal agents escalating chaos and using excessive and lethal force just because they think they can get away with it.
When law enforcement operates without transparency or restraint, people get hurt, families get traumatized, and trust in government gets shattered.
ICE should not be operating like an occupying force in our communities. We need transparency and accountability, and an end to the fear and terror ICE brings into immigrant neighborhoods across the country. While we work to find out more about what happened today, I’m going to keep demanding answers and fighting for policies that put human rights and the safety of our communities first.
In solidarity,
Pramila Jayapal

Yesterday's special election in New Britain should have been a wake-up call for Connecticut Republicans--and for anyone who believes voter engagement still matters.
[Pledge your support](https://substack..FkJId7GDY05odZ4DGOWVdpAPpIqV4lMkJcSiKOGuN6Q?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=183856635)
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=1454853&post_id=183856635&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTgzODU2NjM1LCJpYXQiOjE3Njc4MzI3NDYsImV4cCI6MTc3MDQyNDc0NiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTE0NTQ4NTMiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.foyxgx5k50KxWaX24w5C7fsYFjkC_mPAOelRuClWMNc)
The race pitted Republican **Jamie Vaughan** against Democrat **Iris Noemi S anchez**. Turnout was strikingly low: **fewer than 600 voters** cast ballots.
The results were as follows:
* **Iris Noemi S anchez (D): 365 votes**
* **Jamie Vaughan (R): 181 votes**

This outcome is especially frustrating given the context. Vaughan previously ran for the same seat in 2024 and earned **1,543 votes** , just under 30 percent of the total. Had even **40 percent of those prior supporters turned out** in Tuesday's special election, Vaughan would have won.
They didn't--and that is the real story.
* * *
### A Systemic Engagement Failure
What happened in New Britain reflects a broader, recurring problem in Connecticut politics: **when there is a real opportunity to flip a seat, voters often do not show up --or do not even know the election is happening**.
That failure is particularly striking given that **New Britain is home to gubernatorial candidate Erin Stewart**. Vaughan qualified for the **Citizens ' Election Program (CEP) for $27,000 ** and had visible institutional backing, including Stewart's support. Yet even with name recognition, resources, and leadership nearby, turnout barely registered.
This is not about one candidate or one endorsement. It points to a deeper issue: **organizational follow-through and voter activation are breaking down** , even in places where conditions should favor engagement.
* * *
### The Numbers Tell the Story
The contrast could not be clearer. In **November 2024** , **5,157 voters** cast ballots in this district. On Tuesday, that number collapsed to **just over 500**.
What makes this even more baffling is that Connecticut now offers **early voting and online absentee ballot requests** , tools specifically designed to make participation easier. And still, special elections routinely attract only a fraction of the electorate.
Special elections should be opportunities. Instead, they are being squandered.
* * *
### Another Test Next Week
This issue will be tested again almost immediately.
Next week, a special election will be held in the **139th Assembly District** , covering parts of **Ledyard, Montville, and Norwich**. Democrat **Larry Pemberton Jr.** , also endorsed by the Working Families Party, will face Republican **Brandon Sabbag**.
Early voting for the **January 13 election** will be available from **January 8 -11**, between **10 a.m. and 6 p.m.**
In the 2024 general election, **10,799 voters** turned out in this district.
The question now is simple--and troubling:
Will turnout again collapse into the hundreds?
* * *
### A Call to Action, Not Infighting
**This is not about creating infighting within the Republican Party, favoring one gubernatorial candidate over another, or assigning blame after the fact. It is a call to action.**
Special elections are won on awareness and turnout. If you know voters in these towns, if you are connected to local Republican Town Committees, or if you are part of grassroots networks, there is a responsibility to **apply pressure where it matters: getting voters to the polls when a seat is truly in play**.
In New Britain, **Jamie Vaughan could have won**. With modest engagement, that seat could have flipped--**nudging the Democratic supermajority back, even if only slightly**. Those margins matter. Every seat matters.
The lesson here is not ideological. It is operational.
If parties want to win special elections, they must do more than nominate candidates or issue endorsements. They must **communicate urgency** , **activate local networks** , and **treat special elections as what they are: rare, high-impact opportunities**.
Otherwise, the result in New Britain will not be an exception. It will be the rule.
And that should concern everyone--regardless of party.

body:
Real leaders show up where families need help |
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/122872635/593747465/-1181810701?refcode=WUEFHM05_20260107_HWW3_PL_v1s3&sourceid=1057537&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNRUwvMS84NzA2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzMmY2MzY5YS0yYWVjLWYwMTEtODE5NS0wMDBkM2ExZDU4YWEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=LJy6JNxHQ9rwdiEBugmLKZK_v9BYCrdZjguCUEhTK-k=) Peter, when Hurricane Harvey overwhelmed Houston, I was serving on City Council. It was immediately clear that many families could not safely leave their homes, secure medication, or reach essential resources. I did not wait for press conferences or cameras. I put on my boots and knocked on doors to check on seniors, disabled neighbors, parents with young children, and people who were entirely alone.

Community members told me later that they were surprised to see an elected official show up in person, but to me, this is the foundation of public service. Representation is not symbolic. It must be lived. It must meet people where their needs are.

For nearly a year, Houston has gone without a representative in Congress. Families who needed help navigating immigration challenges, federal aid, healthcare appeals, or small-business survival had no congressional office to call. They were left without support because Gov. Greg Abbott chose partisan politics over basic service.

I am running for Congress because representation must be rooted in accountability, responsiveness, and dignity. I believe deeply that government must deliver for everyday people — those who are working hard, caring for family members, building businesses, raising children, navigating rising costs, or planning for retirement.

I have lived these realities myself. When my father battled cancer, my family spent months worried about whether insurance would come through and whether we would be able to afford care. No family should face that kind of fear — and no one should face it alone.

I have approached public service with a focus on outcomes. On City Council, I helped expand access to capital for women and minority entrepreneurs, strengthen public transit systems, and support small businesses throughout our community. I believe in governing with preparation, humility, and a commitment to responsibility.

This runoff election will determine whether Houston has a representative who listens, shows up, and delivers. clean_body: Real leaders show up where families need help | = Peter, when Hurricane Harvey overwhelmed Houston, I was serving on City Council. It was immediately clear that many families could not safely leave their homes, secure medication, or reach essential resources. I did not wait for press conferences or cameras. I put on my boots and knocked on doors to check on seniors, disabled neighbors, parents with young children, and people who were entirely alone. Community members told me later that they were surprised to see an elected official show up in person, but to me, this is the foundation of public service. Representation is not symbolic. It must be lived. It must meet people where their needs are. For nearly a year, Houston has gone without a representative in Congress. Families who needed help navigating immigration challenges, federal aid, healthcare appeals, or small-business survival had no congressional office to call. They were left without support because Gov. Greg Abbott chose partisan politics over basic service. I am running for Congress because representation must be rooted in accountability, responsiveness, and dignity. I believe deeply that government must deliver for everyday people — those who are working hard, caring for family members, building businesses, raising children, navigating rising costs, or planning for retirement. I have lived these realities myself. When my father battled cancer, my family spent months worried about whether insurance would come through and whether we would be able to afford care. No family should face that kind of fear — and no one should face it alone. I have approached public service with a focus on outcomes. On City Council, I helped expand access to capital for women and minority entrepreneurs, strengthen public transit systems, and support small businesses throughout our community. I believe in governing with preparation, humility, and a commitment to responsibility. This runoff election will determine whether Houston has a representative who listens, shows up, and delivers. To reach voters across TX-18, I need to build the grassroots runway that this moment requires. **= If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue, your donation will go through immediately: | = | = ---|--- = | = = | = Thank you for believing in what representation can be when it is anchored in real service and real accountability. A decade after Judicial Watch reported that Medicaid, the
government’ s fraud-infested health insurance program for the needy,
spent $26 million to provide dead people in one state alone with
benefits, a federal audit reveals the problem continues full-throttle
with hundreds of millions of dollars in “unallowable payments” on
behalf of “deceased enrollees.” It is an unbelievable story that
illustrates government inefficiency, especially when it involves
welfare programs. The waste has been well documented for many years,
yet little has been done to correct the problem. With an annual budget
of about $900 billion Medicaid is jointly funded by federal and state
governments. The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS)
administers the program at the federal level and states have
CMS-approved plans to run their Medicaid programs, which provide
low-income residents with medical coverage. In some states the
government contracts with insurance companies and makes fixed monthly
payments to provide coverage.

The waste has been well documented for many years, yet little has been done to correct the problem. With an annual budget of about $900 billion Medicaid is jointly funded by federal and state governments. The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) administers the program at the federal level and states have CMS-approved plans to run their Medicaid programs, which provide low-income residents with medical coverage. In some states the government contracts with insurance companies and makes fixed monthly payments to provide coverage. name: Mallory McMorrow
subject: What I said to Brian Tyler Cohen
body:
[ https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/685?t=1001&akid=3568%2E898137%2ENeZ5km ][IMG]

Team,

I recently sat down with Brian Tyler Cohen to talk about this race for the
Senate. Before I dive into what I shared, I’m going to ask the thing you
probably expect at this point:

[ https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/107?c0=mam-em-janvideo2026.CCflH_&refcode=AU_MAM_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260107_PM2_V1_S1&t=1002&akid=3568%2E898137%2ENeZ5km ]Will you chip in to help power our campaign for U.S. Senate?

I know, I know. Fundraising emails aren’t anyone’s favorite. But the truth
is, your support is what makes everything I’m about to tell you possible.

[ https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/4?c0=mam-em-janvideo2026.j3j4X7&refcode=AU_MAM_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260107_PM2_V1_S1&t=1003&akid=3568%2E898137%2ENeZ5km ]Mallory McMorrow and Brian Tyler Cohen

Here’s what I told Brian:

Since I got into this race in April, I’ve jumped more than 10 points in
the polls — and I’m the only candidate who’s gaining. That didn’t happen
by accident.

We’re doing up to a dozen events every single week. We’re traveling all
across Michigan. We’re showing up in union halls, coffee shops, breweries,
living rooms — wherever people are. We’re active everywhere you actually
get information: traditional media, social media, and face-to-face
conversations.

Most importantly, we’re listening. We’re building this campaign together
with Michiganders, not handing down talking points from a consultant memo.

And that’s exactly what it’s going to take to beat Mike Rogers.

Just last week, Rogers went on a (different) podcast and admitted his
entire strategy. Not to reach out to all Michiganders. Not to listen to
people or figure out how to solve the problems they’re facing.

His plan? Get 80% of the people who voted for him last year to vote for
him again. That’s it. Tens of millions of dollars are already being
funneled into this state to prop up that strategy.

What we’re doing is different. And it’s working. But make no mistake: this
race is going to be close, expensive, and relentless. The only way we win
is if we keep showing up everywhere, and that’s only possible with your
support.

[ https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/126?c0=mam-em-janvideo2026.8oeo9V&refcode=AU_MAM_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260107_PM2_V1_S1&t=1004&akid=3568%2E898137%2ENeZ5km ]So I’m asking again: Will you chip in $5, $10, or whatever you can
today to help us keep building the kind of campaign Michigan deserves?

If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your
donation will go through immediately:

[ https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/7?c0=mam-em-janvideo2026.nMpp90&refcode=AU_MAM_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260107_PM2_V1_S1&t=1005&akid=3568%2E898137%2ENeZ5km ]CHIP IN $10 NOW

[ https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/8?c0=mam-em-janvideo2026.ILYqXI&refcode=AU_MAM_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260107_PM2_V1_S1&t=1006&akid=3568%2E898137%2ENeZ5km ]CHIP IN $25 NOW

[ https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/9?c0=mam-em-janvideo2026.AdyDkE&refcode=AU_MAM_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260107_PM2_V1_S1&t=1007&akid=3568%2E898137%2ENeZ5km ]CHIP IN $50 NOW

[ https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/10?c0=mam-em-janvideo2026.loGRth&refcode=AU_MAM_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260107_PM2_V1_S1&t=1008&akid=3568%2E898137%2ENeZ5km ]CHIP IN $100 NOW

[ https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/12?c0=mam-em-janvideo2026.T6ZFbE&refcode=AU_MAM_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260107_PM2_V1_S1&t=1009&akid=3568%2E898137%2ENeZ5km ]CHIP IN $250 NOW

[ https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/701?c0=mam-em-janvideo2026.2UG741&refcode=AU_MAM_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260107_PM2_V1_S1&t=1010&akid=3568%2E898137%2ENeZ5km ]ANOTHER AMOUNT

Thank you for being part of this. This is grassroots momentum versus big
money, and I’m betting on us every time.

—Mallory

Peter,

Long before I ever put on a badge, I made a simple promise to myself:

When something is broken, you don't complain - _you fix it._

That philosophy guided me through eight years as Sheriff. It's why I stood up to cartels, why I defended our border communities, and why I backed our deputies even when it wasn't politically convenient.

But today, something bigger is broken.

Washington has stopped listening to the people who make this country work. Not the lobbyists. Not the bureaucrats. _The people_.

The ranchers who wake up before dawn. The small business owners who sign both sides of the paycheck. The parents who are fighting to protect their kids' future. The families who still believe in God, Family, and Freedom.

They deserve a voice that won't fold when things get tough.

**That's why I'm running for Congress - not to join the political class, but to challenge it.** To restore the kind of leadership that answers to the people, not to the unelected and unaccountable. And I'm going to fight for that every single day. But I can't do it alone.

clean_body: When something is broken, you don't complain — you fix it. | Peter, Long before I ever put on a badge, I made a simple promise to myself: When something is broken, you don't complain - you fix it. That philosophy guided me through eight years as Sheriff. It's why I stood up to cartels, why I defended our border communities, and why I backed our deputies even when it wasn't politically convenient. But today, something bigger is broken. Washington has stopped listening to the people who make this country work. Not the lobbyists. Not the bureaucrats. The people. The ranchers who wake up before dawn. The small business owners who sign both sides of the paycheck. The parents who are fighting to protect their kids' future. The families who still believe in God, Family, and Freedom. They deserve a voice that won't fold when things get tough. That's why I'm running for Congress - not to join the political class, but to challenge it. To restore the kind of leadership that answers to the people, not to the unelected and unaccountable. And I'm going to fight for that every single day. But I can't do it alone. body:
It’s about scaring the people of this country into silence. I didn’t get shot at and launch into orbit to see freedom of speech in the United States end on my watch.
#

Team,
Trump and Hegseth are coming after everything I worked for over 25 years in the Navy and NASA.
That’s true.
But this is about more than just me. It’s about scaring the people of this country into silence.
I didn’t get shot at and launch into orbit to see freedom of speech in the United States end on my watch.
I am not going to be silenced. I am going to fight them tooth and nail over this. I won’t let them make an example out of me, and I absolutely won’t let them intimidate everyone else.
Ain’t gonna happen.
But to win against these bullies I need a couple things.
First off, I need a massive team from coast-to-coast that’s not afraid and is ready to speak out against Trump.
And second, we’re going to need to raise a significant amount of resources — not just to fight Hegseth and what he’s trying to do to me, but to protect the rights of every American. To take back our majorities in Congress and reign in this lawless president. To defend our democracy and our Constitution, just like I swore an oath to do 40 years ago.
I don’t need you to chip in to every email I send, but I am hoping you might give to this one.

[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/PNG%202023%20TOP%20Newsletter%20Header.png]
Lea el boletín en español abajo [#Español]
DON'T MISS IT:
ACA Healthcare Marketplace open enrollment deadline is Jan. 15
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Family%20healthcare%20stock.jpeg]
You still have time: January 15 is the final deadline for the Health Insurance Marketplace Open Enrollment Period (OEP) [https://www.healthcare.gov/quick-guide/dates-and-deadlines/] for 2026 coverage. While the president and congressional Republicans continue to fail us when it comes to making healthcare more affordable, there are still steps marketplace shoppers can take to ensure they make informed choices for an upcoming plan.
At TOP, we believe healthcare is a human right, and that it’s central to vibrant families and communities. Every person – no matter their background – should have access to quality care.
https://health.usnews.com/wellness/articles/how-to-pick-a-health-insurance-plan [https://health.usnews.com/wellness/articles/how-to-pick-a-health-insurance-plan]
Ready to celebrate the life and legacy of a civil rights icon
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/MLK%20waving.jpg]
Come join us! TOP staff and members will participate in celebrations taking place soon to honor the vision and impact of Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr.
TOP’s fight for racial and economic justice is intrinsically linked to Dr. King’s bold, unapologetic vision for revolutionary change through nonviolent resistance.
Interested in celebrating with us? Email Andres at arodriguez@organizetexas.org [arodriguez@organizetexas.org] for details on the MLK events TOP plans to attend.
Never forgetting:
Condemning Trump and MAGA's coup attempt on Jan. 6
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Capitol%20Jan%206%20light.jpg]
No amount of gaslighting will ever hide the fact that five years ago Donald Trump and MAGA plotted a coup to overturn the will of voters after he lost the 2020 presidential election. Millions across the country that day witnessed on televisions and smartphone screens mobs violently try to dismantle our democracy – the very democracy that Trump is now chipping away at through cruel policies targeting entire communities and our nation’s most marginalized.
TOP knows that Texas is ground zero in the fight to defend democracy. In our state alone, more than 100 Texans were directly involved in this attack on January 6, the state with the second most insurrectionists. [https://www.texastribune.org/2025/01/21/texans-insurrection-capitol-trump-pardon/] From our governor to our senators, representatives, and local officials, far too many Texas Republicans to this day remain complicit with the white nationalist violence that transpired. No matter your age, race, gender, faith, nationality, or income, we unapologetically organize for a vision where every person can prosper and is guaranteed the dignity they deserve, as well as a future where those who try to trample our rights are actually held accountable.
While Trump and MAGA seek to pit people against one another, TOP is working to build bridges, foster community, and advance justice.
TOP Tip: Doomscroll less to boost your mental health in 2026
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Smartphone%20detox%20screen%20time.jpg]
With news of all sorts hitting us at all hours of the day in these times — from the trivial to the abysmal — it's not a bad idea to start the new year on a quieter note by reducing your personal screen time. Check out these tips on how you can do your mind and body good through a doomscroll detox. [https://www.theguardian.com/thefilter-us/2026/jan/06/how-to-reduce-phone-screen-time]
Español
NO TE LO PIERDAS:
La fecha límite para inscribirse en el Mercado de Seguros Médicos es el 15 de enero
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Family%20healthcare%20stock.jpeg]
Todavía estás a tiempo: el 15 de enero es la fecha límite para inscribirse en el Mercado de Seguros Médicos [https://www.cuidadodesalud.gov/es/quick-guide/dates-and-deadlines/] para obtener cobertura en 2026. Aunque el presidente y los republicanos en el Congreso continúan fallándonos cuando se trata de hacer el cuidado de la salud más accesible, todavía hay pasos que las personas pueden tomar para asegurarse de tomar decisiones informadas al elegir un plan.
En TOP, creemos que la atención médica es un derecho humano y que es fundamental para familias y comunidades prósperas. Todas las personas, sin importar su origen, deben tener acceso a atención médica de calidad.
http://health.usnews.com/wellness/articles/how-to-pick-a-health-insurance-plan [http://health.usnews.com/wellness/articles/how-to-pick-a-health-insurance-plan]
Listos para celebrar la vida y el legado de un ícono de los derechos civiles
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/MLK%20waving.jpg]
¡Únete a nosotros! El personal y los miembros de TOP participarán en las celebraciones que se llevarán a cabo próximamente para honrar la visión y el legado del Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr.
La lucha de TOP por la justicia racial y económica está intrínsecamente ligada a la visión audaz e inquebrantable del Dr. King de un cambio revolucionario a través de la resistencia no violenta.
¿Te interesa celebrar con nosotros? Envía un correo electrónico a Andres a arodriguez@organizetexas.org [arodriguez@organizetexas.org] para obtener más información sobre los eventos de MLK a los que TOP planea asistir.
Nunca lo olvídaremos:
Condenando el intento de golpe de Estado de Trump y MAGA del 6 de enero
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Capitol%20Jan%206%20light.jpg]
Ninguna manipulación ni intento de distorsionar la realidad podrá ocultar el hecho de que hace cinco años Donald Trump y el movimiento MAGA planearon un golpe de Estado para anular la voluntad de los votantes tras su derrota en las elecciones presidenciales de 2020. Millones de personas en todo el país presenciaron ese día, a través de la televisión y las pantallas de sus teléfonos, cómo turbas intentaban violentamente desmantelar nuestra democracia,la misma democracia que Trump ahora sigue debilitando mediante políticas crueles que atacan a comunidades enteras y a las personas más marginadas de nuestra nación.
TOP sabe que Texas es el epicentro de la lucha por la defensa de la democracia. Solo en nuestro estado, más de 100 tejanos estuvieron directamente involucrados en este ataque del 6 de enero, siendo Texas el segundo estado con mayor número de insurrectos. [https://www.texastribune.org/2025/01/21/texans-insurrection-capitol-trump-pardon/] Desde nuestro gobernador hasta nuestros senadores, representantes y funcionarios locales, demasiados republicanos de Texas siguen siendo cómplices de la violencia nacionalista blanca que se desató. Sin importar la edad, raza, género, religión, nacionalidad o ingresos, nos organizamos sin reservas por una visión en la que cada persona pueda prosperar y se le garantice la dignidad que merece, así como un futuro en el que quienes intentan pisotear nuestros derechos rindan cuentas por sus actos.
Mientras Trump y el movimiento MAGA buscan dividir a la gente, TOP trabaja para construir puentes, fomentar la comunidad y promover la justicia .
Consejos de TOP: Dedica menos tiempo a tu teléfono para mejorar tu salud mental
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Smartphone%20detox%20screen%20time.jpg]
En estos tiempos, con noticias de todo tipo que nos llegan a todas horas del día —desde las más triviales hasta las más terribles—, no es mala idea empezar el año con más tranquilidad reduciendo el tiempo que pasamos frente a las pantallas. Consulta estos consejos para cuidar tu mente y tu cuerpo con una desintoxicación digital. [https://www.theguardian.com/thefilter-us/2026/jan/06/how-to-reduce-phone-screen-time]

name: Team McBride
subject: Urgent: Our health care system is facing a crisis
disclaimer_text: Paid for by McBride for Delaware
body:
We can still act.
#
**Right now, our health care system is facing a crisis.**
Republicans in Congress let the Affordable Care Act subsidies expire on December 31.
Now, premiums are skyrocketing, and millions of families are facing monthly insurance rates that have doubled. Others are being forced to go without coverage.
And it’s about to get worse.
Trump-era Medicaid cuts are set to take effect soon, stripping coverage from millions more and putting even more pressure on hospitals, caregivers, and working families just trying to afford care — all so Republicans can fund tax breaks for billionaires.
But we can still act.
**The House is voting as soon as TOMORROW on legislation to extend ACA subsidies, and we need your voice to put pressure on Congress to pass it.**
**[Can you add your name to demand that Congress extend these ACA insurance subsidies ASAP and protect coverage for millions of Americans?](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/sign/em-20260107-aca-subsidies/?source=em20260107-2657&t=1&akid=2657%2E21716%2EON6hlr)**
**[ADD YOUR NAME](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/sign/em-20260107-aca-subsidies/?source=em20260107-2657&t=2&akid=2657%2E21716%2EON6hlr)**
Thank you,
Team McBride

body:
#
What happened today in Minnesota is a nightmare.
This is what we've been warning about for a very long time.
It's tragic to say, but from the moment that this Congress decided to authorize and explode ICE's budget, they became accountable to no one.
It's important that people know that ICE has less accountability than virtually any law enforcement agency in the United States — yet they are some of the most well-funded, they are operating with impunity, and we just saw them murder an American citizen in cold blood in the street.
Despite whatever lies the President wants to say, you can see what happened for yourselves: they shot a woman, in the head, in cold blood, on the street.
**I hope that this incident is prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law**.
This is an agency that must be reined in.
In solidarity,
Alexandria

It’s time for common sense—not chaos—in Congress.

Hi Peter, Let's be honest: the so-called **" One Big Beautiful Bill"** isn't helping the American people--it's hurting us. **It handed billions in tax breaks to the wealthiest Americans.****
****It gutted protections for Medicare and Medicaid.****
****It ballooned the deficit --all while working families struggle to get by.** This wasn't a bill for the people. It was a payoff for the powerful. And if we don't push back now, the damage will only get worse. I'm John Vincent, and I'm running for Congress in South Carolina's 7th District to bring some **common sense back to Washington.** I spent 20 years in the Navy and built a small business from the ground up--but I've never seen working families under this much pressure. I believe we can do better--**if we fight back and flip seats like this one.** Here's what I'll do in Congress:
* **Work to reverse the worst parts of this bill** --starting with the tax giveaways
* **Protect Medicare, Medicaid, and SNAP** from future cuts
* **Invest in working-class communities, not just the donor class****

**

But I can't do this without your help. **This campaign is people-powered** --no corporate PACs, no billionaire checks. Just folks who are ready to fight for something better. # **Reflections on the Passing of Doug LaMalfa
and Why Running Still Mattered**
---
| | Dear friends,

I was saddened to hear of the sudden passing of Representative Doug LaMalfa. While we strongly disagreed on many issues, I extend my condolences to his family and loved ones during this difficult time.

His passing has prompted me to reflect on why I challenged him for his seat in Congress - especially when the odds were deeply stacked against me.

When I ran against Rep. LaMalfa, many people questioned it and said the race was unwinnable. They weren’t wrong about the math. But they didn’t understand why I felt called to do it.

Progressives don’t run only when victory is guaranteed. We run because people deserve a voice. We run to counter the assumption that power is so entrenched it cannot be changed. And we run so that constituents know there is someone they can rally around - someone with the courage and moral conviction to say that a better future is possible.

Campaigns like ours matter. They give people a voice for their values. They inspire. They become building blocks for future activists and offer shoulders that others one day will stand on.
Resistance is never futile.

Every time someone stands up, especially in places like California’s District 1 where it’s considered hopeless, the political landscape changes, even if slowly. That belief continues to guide me, and it’s why I remain deeply grateful to all of you who stood with me and believed in that larger purpose.
That same commitment to showing up - grounded in **People** , **Peace** , and **Planet** \- is what now carries me forward as I run to represent California’s 2nd Congressional District.

With appreciation and determination,
**Rose

PS. **Every campaign, every conversation, and every act of courage builds the movement that carries us forward - together.

Progressives don’t run only when victory is guaranteed. We run because people deserve a voice. We run to counter the assumption that power is so entrenched it cannot be changed. And we run so that constituents know there is someone they can rally around - someone with the courage and moral conviction to say that a better future is possible. Campaigns like ours matter. They give people a voice for their values. They inspire. They become building blocks for future activists and offer shoulders that others one day will stand on. Resistance is never futile. Every time someone stands up, especially in places like California’s District 1 where it’s considered hopeless, the political landscape changes, even if slowly. That belief continues to guide me, and it’s why I remain deeply grateful to all of you who stood with me and believed in that larger purpose. That same commitment to showing up - grounded in People , Peace , and Planet \- is what now carries me forward as I run to represent California’s 2nd Congressional District. With appreciation and determination, Rose PS. Every campaign, every conversation, and every act of courage builds the movement that carries us forward - together. | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Paid for by Rose for Congress 3335 Placer St # 288 Redding, CA 96001-2364 * USA or |

By Illinois Review

Illinois politics has a long history of blurred ethical lines, but the latest episode involving Wirepoints pushes those boundaries into legally dangerous territory.

Wirepoints, a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization, has published a political attack piece targeting Republican gubernatorial candidate Darren Bailey – while its former president, Ted Dabrowski, is running for the same office in the 2026 Republican primary.
https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2026/01/tax-exempt-wirepoints-breaks-irs-rules-to-smear-bailey-and-boost-dabrowskis-governor-run.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=b2f7432604-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_10_30_09_24_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-8b40ac336f-666344823
Dabrowski appeared to recognize this reality in September 2025, when he resigned as president of Wirepoints, explicitly citing the need to comply with 501(c)(3) restrictions ahead of his gubernatorial campaign.

Shortly thereafter, he formally announced his candidacy, named a running mate, and began raising campaign funds.

But resignation alone does not erase conflicts of interest.

An institution that believed it was above accountability. **They were wrong. And we have the footage to prove it.** Here are five investigations from 2025 that changed the game:
* **1\. THE $100 BILLION FEDERAL CONTRACTING SCAM (October)**
* We exposed ATI Government Solutions exploiting the SBA's 8(a) minority contracting program -- outsourcing 80% of their work while pocketing over $100 million in no-bid contracts. This wasn't a one-off. It was a systemic scheme across multiple agencies.
* **THE RESULT:** SBA suspension. $253 million in contracts halted. A $9 billion Treasury Department audit. Seven additional companies suspended. And a 15-year review of 8(a) contracts across every federal agency.
* **2\. GAO DATA THEFT CONFESSION (November)**
* A GAO director admitted on hidden camera that staff "stole and backed up" vaccine data specifically to block RFK Jr.'s HHS reforms. They weren't just resisting policy -- they were breaking federal law.
* **THE RESULT:** The director's profile was scrubbed. A federal investigation was launched. And the nation finally saw what "deep state resistance" actually looks like.
* **3\. NIH PORTRAIT DESTRUCTION (December)**
* NIH contractor Joseph Olmert confessed on camera to destroying official portraits of President Trump, Vice President Vance, RFK Jr., and Dr. Jay Bhattacharya. That's a potential 10-year federal felony -- destruction of government property.
* **THE RESULT:** Contractor FIRED. NIH internal investigation launched. And a national conversation about the defiance embedded in our federal agencies.
* **4\. GEORGETOWN PROFESSOR EXPOSED (December)**
* We caught a Georgetown professor on hidden camera calling Black conservatives "coons" and mocking "stupid white people." When we confronted him, he tried to assault our cameraman. Police were called.
* **THE RESULT:** Georgetown wiped his bio from their website. The footage went viral -- over 2 million views. And elite academic bias was laid bare for all to see.
* **5\. INSIDE EPSTEIN 'S ISLAND (May-December)**
* We released the first-ever footage from inside Jeffrey Epstein's private island mansion. We confronted a DOJ Deputy Chief who admitted plans to redact Republicans from the Epstein files. We published unredacted photos that Democrats tried to hide.
* **THE RESULT:** DOJ was forced to respond. Media outlets issued corrections. Joe Rogan covered our findings. And the truth about elite corruption reached millions who had been kept in the dark.

Peter, I recently visited Sedgwick Health center in Julesburg, Colorado. They serve seniors, run the local nursing home and keep their ER open around the clock. According to the hospital, 80% of their patients rely on Medicaid and Medicare. But now that the GOP's "Big, Beautiful Bill" has become law, Sedgwick will lose 25% of its Medicaid reimbursement - and all of their services might not survive it. Lauren Boebert voted for this. She voted to gut the care her constituents depend on. I know firsthand how critical accessible health care is for Coloradan families. I fought tooth and nail to get my parents the care they needed when they were both diagnosed with cancer. No one should have to beg for help when they're sick or struggling - but that's exactly the reality Boebert just voted for.
As one rural hospital CEO put it: "Where you live shouldn't determine if you live." He's right. And I'll never stop working to ensure our neighbors get the care they need - no matter their ZIP code. That's why I'm on the road - meeting with hospital leaders, families and local officials who know what's really at stake. But this kind of campaign takes resources, Seth. Every trip we take, every ad we place, every door we knock on - it's all powered by grassroots folks like you. Dear Peter,
# Elections deserve scrutiny. Anomalies deserve review. Americans deserve confidence in their elections this new year!
When transparency is blocked, isn’t that reason enough to ask harder questions? Unite4Freedom has a mission, and it isn’t about parties or outcomes — it’s about restoring trust and confidence in the validity of our election process. ## US Seizes Russian Oil Tanker at Sea
The U.S. Coast Guard seized two sanctioned ships Wednesday morning, one a [Russian-flagged oil tanker,](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFuwyAYxfHTwOYIvhhMBoYu3tK1o-WYR0xLwDIklnP6Ks0ROj_pL_3e13k4jyGGdP0cb7DV5yFhKxG1Yh3upSA8UeqYfrCWhM3n7JZ9HUiQboRshBncGOI-tNxZDxCOHFZ2ujOdaCXx2ToYLyXpbvJKnvTkQJKO3jsvcIEyPNhXTUhhpBRaiYNx7WSMMvIk_IWUYq2ACzWvh-8cUp3h454fWA9TvvFo51qXwo4fjHpGfZ0xhxhfG6N-yTFMO6PewSMVMOqV7jQZ2dxL89Y1DyQ874hj84Yy6vlq3bKFGEPRHWvF9TaGvyav_zrpYek3AAD__xiGe_w) after a dramatic chase across the Atlantic, despite that ship being shadowed by a Russian submarine. Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem said the vessel had [changed flags and names](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2O3CAURp8Gd4wA_zEFxUSRm2jTJFFKi4HLzk0wWFy8ZPL0kbOPsPWRPn3n_HxZXyxGTK9f7QamhrwmaBShVijrQQT4F6ja9BsKJWghZ78_y6qEmriQXOjVW4zPdei8CQAK-g6MnKdZz2KQqnuYEaT0bgrWwn20_q6nadR6dv0VgnZX6NCca0IKLaWYRnHRfnBaj1peRbircWSDAI81l8uvjKk-IMRnfoNycXnronnUuhPrb0wtTC2ttctG6WRMLZD4QUwtp9QJc4meqeUg7iEgEN8yudz4uyfPGPm7LPdAO1bg5SBCmzgd980WTMCBXC6VqcUWfrvJ719-bH9Yv2SHnvWfP50todE3KHtXjN8bxog0zWwQr5vF-P91_VDqN6P-BQAA__-d5JaB) to avoid capture while attempting to pick up sanctioned Venezuelan oil. The operation, supported by [U.S. and British surveillance](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkEFuhCAYRk-DOwwgCrNgMU3Dpplu2qRLg_KrtAgGcMz09I3tEbp-yZfvvY9bfzPOuzC_mhVUmWIf4MgeSoHU7zmD-4ZcTPiClAMcU4x2e6SeEdZhQjGRvTXOP3peWTUBMGgqUFR0QgrCKasWRYXklFILzIwUmuZCBFhuCDeD6YQYKqfONUKJpJR0Laml5aOUraQXMg2sbREnYF2Jqf6MLpQFJv-Id0j1GNfKq6WULaPmiphGTB_HUa85nAwxDQHvGTF9Sp0wJm8R09teXMAWJgcZl7SvG04wm2RdmPEA3htMcXQe_5kjpk3C1yt9f6GLRo2Oo7OoeX46u8GR3yBtVVJ2O5z3LncCcTKvxvnfh-VfWe-K_QQAAP__MB6M0w) near Iceland and Scotland, marked a rare direct standoff between U.S. ships and a Russian-escorted vessel. A second, stateless tanker was also seized in the Caribbean as the U.S. aims to block oil trade among Venezuela, Russia, Iran, and China.
## ICE Agent Fatally Shoots Woman in Minneapolis
Renee Nicole Good, a 37-year-old Minneapolis woman, was [shot and killed by an ICE agent](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0M1uhCAUxfGnwR0G8ANcsOjG3XTbpUG5jrQIhntHM336Zpr0Cbr-Jye_nI_bdHMhhnR_dztYWvOU4MIIRFCmByKEb0By6QsKJrjWnP3xLJMSqudCcmEm70J8Tm3l7QqgoKnASt1ro0UrVbXZvnPdPCy69w1ooaHxc6OFaZvB63WQqgr2tSakMFKKvhO18e1iTGfkINZZdR1rBfhAudSfOSTaYI3PfEKpl7xX0W5EB7LmjamRqfG6rnqZX1Z8dabGPaQEmMkxNcZwAn8c3hHgX3JHjgH5Ch6Ki9zdIRHyo2QCJCjIl-hw40cuFF3y3J2QHsDUWBXrjyvEGLDXrBX33YX4i6J_PXla9RMAAP__qriLRQ) Wednesday morning during a federal immigration operation in south Minneapolis, triggering protests and sharply conflicting accounts. Federal officials say Good drove her SUV into an agent near 34th Street and Portland Avenue; President Trump shared video of the incident and said the officer was “viciously” run over and is now hospitalized. [See the footage here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1u6zAUg5_G3hRIsv4yaLhLtty1o6FER_FpZMmwTmO4T1-4KPoC3T6ABAny7TpeA2Ysj_9hBk-pjgW2loEI1vGjNcBPaBTKE9ZWYEu1xmVfR8mlYVww7sYYMO-j6qNPABKGHrywxjrLlZD95JVI55i0VgZ4sHbQA0-Di-ZsXbiFYHr0RxoX3AnBjeYnF9XdOe3Emaeb1LpTHCJSXU_vFQtNkPJeX7Ce7nXus5-IltYN_zp56eTl2Wg5hB9kx5xOXqj-It6BhQcUYm2qlRp7Ys6NbXUOhWFhM5YCYakZD3e_-rhsmDM2YzvFH3PA_N1Mf7rr5eVXAAAA___48YBI) (_Warning: graphic content_). State and city leaders dispute that version. Minneapolis Mayor Jacob Frey [bluntly rebutted the official account](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFyhCAURb9GOxxgFbGgSGO3aVM6rDzWt4vg8Ng15usz5hdSn7l3zr1f1-lqMWC8f9oVTPFpirBTgFIgTy8iwB-gYuMTMkXYfUpuO_IkuVSMC8b15CyGY2prZzyAhEsNRvSq1z1vhawXI4bezlb7YQCnOzHftBAX65z1SirlXY3mbOOCayG46nijXTtr3WkxcH-TXVe1HByWlJtHwlgW8OFIb8jNnNY6mKWUjarLRyXHSo77vjc-fQ8nrOR4rqnkuGKMYLcUkNhqj5QZzsBoSalgvDOC4JkDD5GA3V4h0IKFJe9xRhuI7RgCI4Ane7yonNGHjezUrrNx24mRVF-1_L5aDH9i5V9vvo38DQAA__95z4zG), which described officers as "fearing for their life" before shooting into the victim’s vehicle. _"They are already trying to spin this as an act of self-defense,"_ Frey said. _"Having seen the video myself, I want to tell everybody directly: that is bulls—."_ The shooting drew protesters within hours, just blocks from the site of George Floyd’s killing in 2020. The FBI and Minnesota Bureau of Criminal Apprehension are investigating.
## RFK Jr. Unveils 'Upside Down' Food Pyramid
The Trump administration [released new Dietary Guidelines](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGu3CAQRb8Gd6wG1ja8giKNu02b0sJmvJ4EAwK8lvP1EfmF10wzV0f33F-v-WXJU3j_tAeausU54FU81op5PktB-oul2vAHcwl4bTG6dOdZghw5CA56dpb8PfedMxuixGeHRqhRaQW9kN1uhtUqAb3dFuXs-vxalHNWgVyXUQOsuiPTaCBACwHjAA_t-lXrQYsv2BY5DKwHdFRjfvyOFOqOm7_jB_NjjUfnzV5rKuz5g8mJySncKZbaXkxODczkBKIdxeR0Ft78mJxqPo_ErTso8HrmQOHNmx1Pd7YHOX6mQg65i1fg6Sx7C6QcK1Lgm62N0WXj0kXeUxkV6-F9WPL_W9VvTfkx8l8AAAD___tIiVA) for Americans that "turn the food pyramid upside down," emphasizing protein and healthy fats, while limiting added sugar and ultra-processed foods. Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. said the guidelines replace "corporate-driven assumptions" and recommended [potentially doubling protein](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u3CAQRp8Gd1jM-AduQREpstLctCkt1oztSTCsAK_lPH20eYVbf9Knc86vz_nTceC4_XQH2bqmOdJVAtVKeT5LIf5Lpbr4h3KJdK0p-eedZ1Q4SgVSmdk7DvfcN96uREhdQxb0qI1WPWCzWw_DMj5A94ZAA2GHGnAxg-nJIYBv2L7fFCgDoMZBtcb3izGDgQ-1PnAYRK_Ic025_Z041p3WcKcX5XZJRxPsXuuziO6bwEng5B7L26Dd0nsWOP0gF-oucLp2riT3dBaSmQK5QkVGuqRnqi7fcjvZU-BIRVJc0pndxnGT7qDMi4tF4FRqyrfoJvai-w5oPvQIaJps_fPiELiMWvRqOxyH_3T1S0lfFv8FAAD__yY4i8I) consumption from 0.8 grams to 1.2-1.6 grams per kilogram of body weight. A kilogram is 2.2 pounds. The 10-page document reintroduces an inverted food pyramid, with meat, cheese, and vegetables at the top, departing from the MyPlate visual guide and directly impacting millions of meals served in public schools, military bases, and federal facilities. [Read the guidelines here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykz0FOAyEUgOHTzOxKHhQYWLBoYuqqbl2S5_BoUQoTwDb19KZewQt8-f_3kz9hyqmc3_BKbsTqC917pjGo-e_eKf1QH1i-qPVC91hr2B7NCxB6B3wHxgdM-eHlHFwkErSfyfFFL2YBycV8cWCkoj0KQEuWx6gQNI96RWvREsKc3FMDDoZz0AqYCXI1RhluIX4IpSYJFNKojX3WVMaFYn7UGzW21uuc3WWMrU_7wySOkziuobBGmJ-l7Fxvkzi-vB7YFuLcXNjuKefU9TJJOF8x5T9j_Gv85sRvAAAA___7jGxi).

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. name: Wes Moore
subject: Why fitness matters to me
body:
Many have been asking me for it.
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=1176%2E1086043%2ECh9SQU)
Peter,
I’m reaching out before I unplug for my daily workout to tell you a little about my routine, and why it’s important. **[And if you could chip in to my campaign while I get after it, I would be very grateful.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260108-1.y1mDiM&refcode=em-20260108-1&t=2&akid=1176%2E1086043%2ECh9SQU)**
I take my physical fitness really seriously. Not just because of my physical health – but because of my mental health, too.
My morning workout is one of the rare times in my day when I get to put down the phone completely, **so it’s become increasingly important to me over the years.**
In my first few weeks as Governor, I was talking with my Chief of Staff about how I would fit workouts into my new schedule. I couldn’t just pop over to the gym anymore – _I was the Governor of a state now._
My Chief reached out to the Naval Academy Superintendent, and to my surprise, they told me I could come by and work out anytime. I thought that was pretty perfect since it was right down the street from our new house.
I met with one of their strength trainers, who offered me a space to work out, but then he gave me an offer I simply could not turn down: If I wanted, I could join the midshipmen in their workouts, too. They welcomed me (not only the Governor, _but also an Army guy!_) without hesitation.
One day, swimming in the pool, I noticed while doing my laps that there were men lying at the bottom of the pool. When I asked the guys I was training with what was going on, they said those men were training to be Navy Seals. I’m no stranger to discipline, so let me tell you — these young men and women at the Naval Academy are the real deal.
So Peter, these morning workouts are vital to me. They keep me centered in the present. They challenge me in unexpected ways that help me show up better for it in my day job.
It’s important to have nonnegotiables in the routine. It’s why I’m unwilling to compromise on my physical fitness, and why I’ll always make time for my family and my faith every single day, no matter what.
So, whatever you’re working on this year – whether it’s building a new workout routine or prioritizing your mental health – commit to it. Protect that time. Make it nonnegotiable.
Elevate,
Wes
[](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260108-1.y1mDiM&refcode=em-20260108-1&t=3&akid=1176%2E1086043%2ECh9SQU)
P.S. **[I have to ask again — will you consider making a donation to my campaign? We need all the help we can get before Maryland’s fundraising freeze takes effect.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260108-1.y1mDiM&refcode=em-20260108-1&t=4&akid=1176%2E1086043%2ECh9SQU)**

I take my physical fitness really seriously. Not just because of my physical health – but because of my mental health, too. My morning workout is one of the rare times in my day when I get to put down the phone completely, so it’s become increasingly important to me over the years. In my first few weeks as Governor, I was talking with my Chief of Staff about how I would fit workouts into my new schedule. I couldn’t just pop over to the gym anymore – I was the Governor of a state now. My Chief reached out to the Naval Academy Superintendent, and to my surprise, they told me I could come by and work out anytime. I thought that was pretty perfect since it was right down the street from our new house. I met with one of their strength trainers, who offered me a space to work out, but then he gave me an offer I simply could not turn down: If I wanted, I could join the midshipmen in their workouts, too. They welcomed me (not only the Governor, but also an Army guy!) without hesitation. One day, swimming in the pool, I noticed while doing my laps that there were men lying at the bottom of the pool. When I asked the guys I was training with what was going on, they said those men were training to be Navy Seals. I’m no stranger to discipline, so let me tell you — these young men and women at the Naval Academy are the real deal. So Peter, these morning workouts are vital to me. They keep me centered in the present. They challenge me in unexpected ways that help me show up better for it in my day job. It’s important to have nonnegotiables in the routine. It’s why I’m unwilling to compromise on my physical fitness, and why I’ll always make time for my family and my faith every single day, no matter what. So, whatever you’re working on this year – whether it’s building a new workout routine or prioritizing your mental health – commit to it. Protect that time. Make it nonnegotiable. Elevate, Wes P.S.

Yesterday, ICE murdered Minnesotan Renee Good in cold blood.
Renee was doing what I've done for my community here in Chicago: legally observing and documenting ICE activity in her city to protect her neighbors from the terror of ICE's brutality.
ICE tried to rip her out of her car, and when she began to drive away, an ICE agent fired several shots into her vehicle, striking her in the head.
Immediately after the incident, DHS Secretary Kristi Noem released statements justifying the shooting and claiming that Renee had tried to hit the agent with her car. Another innocent person murdered by Trump's gestapo.

When Trump launched "Operation Midway Blitz" here, they unleashed hell against my neighbors and I for nothing other than being black or brown. When we protested, they pushed back with thuggish violence, in one instance ramming us with one of their cars and pepper spraying all of us.

ICE needs to be abolished. DHS Secretary Kristi Noem needs to be impeached. ICE agents who have taken part in these crimes against humanity need to be prosecuted.
