ICE shot and killed a 37-year-old American citizen, Renee Nicole Good, in Minneapolis on Wednesday. Renee was in her SUV at an ICE enforcement action and was approached by several armed agents who told her to get out of her car. One agent tried to access her SUV by opening the door. She seemingly panicked and tried to drive away. Another agent, who was partially in her vehicle's path, drew out his gun and lethally shot her twice. The video was recorded by onlookers.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f0299567-01f6-44a5-871f-49ff433b22cf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
As usual, the two sides in our country framed the events very differently. Conservatives said that Renee was a protester assaulting an officer with a deadly weapon, her motor vehicle. Liberals said that ICE agents shot an innocent mother of three in her car for no reason.
In my view, the reality is pretty straightforward. Renee Nicole Good made a poor decision not to obey directions and an even worse one by trying to drive away. But these should not result in instant capital punishment by an armed federal agent. Agents should have the judgment to know when they are dealing with a violent assailant and when they are dealing with a panicking mother behind the wheel of a car.
Even someone who supports ICE activities in communities - which I do not - should be able to regard this as a terrible tragedy and an error in judgment on the part of the agent that led to devastating consequences. The appropriate statement on the part of Republicans should be to express sadness over the violence and say that the facts will come out with an appropriate investigation.
Unfortunately, the polarization in our country makes nuance impossible. Officials characterized Renee Nicole Good as a 'deranged leftist trying to run over a federal agent.' In America today, admitting that your side did something wrong is a sign of weakness and political self-sabotage.
By the way, this applies to both sides. Gavin Newsom is the Democratic frontrunner for 2028 in part because he is demonstrating a willingness to fight fire with fire and be as pugnacious as possible, from slagging Trump online to partisan redistricting to adopting the Bill Clinton insight that "the American people always support strong and wrong versus weak and right."
That sums up the current dynamic. You must appear strong. You can't say your side screwed up because you look weak, which is the biggest sin in 2026. Better to double down and try to shape perception or distort reality and play to your tribe.
It's dehumanizing, which leads to disaster.
To me, the important thing here to remember is the people whose lives have been irrevocably shattered. Renee Nicole Good was a mother of three - three children who will never see their mother again. She wasn't a member of some imagined tribe or a participant in an ideological conflict so much as a living, breathing human being, a wife and mother. She should be alive today. Instead her life was cut short in tragic fashion and turned into an emblem of a conflict that I fear will only grow in intensity and claim more victims in the days ahead. Our shared humanity is the only path out.
To turn down the temperature in our country, check out [Forward](https://substack.com/redirect/453fa433-bcb4-4976-a293-dd38ae67daa8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) which is trying to reduce polarization. To reduce your screen time, which can contribute to polarization in our own lives, check out [Noble Mobile](https://substack.com/redirect/6630dca0-2087-4e16-a3f6-e86e29b25eb4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). We're all still people at the end of the day.

| Dear Fellow American,

Happy New Year from all of us at Judicial Watch. I trust 2026 is off to a strong start for you and your family.
In January, many Americans make resolutions for the new year.
And, as America prepares to celebrate its 250th anniversary, _Judicial Watch is making resolutions too_ ...

* **_We resolve to double down_** on our commitment to the founding principle that no one is above the law.
* **_We resolve to demand a_**** _transparent government_** worthy of our founders' sacrifices.
* **_And we resolve to fight_** tooth and nail through the courts to stop the Radical Left from trying to steal our elections.

With Judicial Watch's 32-year track record of victories, you can trust that our resolutions will be backed up by action (and lawsuits).
And with 140+ active lawsuits in 2026, this year could shape up to be among our most important ever, _which is why keeping our work fully resourced is more critical than ever_.
_[That's why I'm asking you to make a generous first-time donation to our work today](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=78813&L=30946&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL3RoYW5rLXlvdS0yMTYvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPU1heSZ1dG1fdGVybT1Ob24tRG9ub3Jz&hash=aafc90fdace25a5a1871d30fa9a66413e29290f69056683c8a490d5fbaf2a4d2)_.
In 2026, Judicial Watch will:

* **Keep fighting to keep our elections honest** , including our second _United States Supreme Court_ case - to be heard in the next few months - fighting to end the counting of ballots received after Election Day (an open invitation to fraud);

* **Keep leading the fight to clean dirty voter rolls** by suing jurisdictions violating the _National Voter Registration Act_ , building on the 5 million dirty names we have already removed nationwide;

* **Keep working to enforce immigration law** by exposing "sanctuary" obstruction, including our lawsuits in Illinois and Arizona tied to interference with federal immigration enforcement;

* **Keep challenging unconstitutional attacks on equal protection** , including our landmark class-action lawsuit against Evanston, Illinois' race-based reparations program.

And _[with your generous support](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=78813&L=30946&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL3RoYW5rLXlvdS0yMTYvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPU1heSZ1dG1fdGVybT1Ob24tRG9ub3Jz&hash=aafc90fdace25a5a1871d30fa9a66413e29290f69056683c8a490d5fbaf2a4d2)_ , we will stand ready to quickly confront new threats to the rule of law as they appear.
To stand alongside Judicial Watch in 2026, _[please make a generous tax-deductible gift today](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=78813&L=30946&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL3RoYW5rLXlvdS0yMTYvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPU1heSZ1dG1fdGVybT1Ob24tRG9ub3Jz&hash=aafc90fdace25a5a1871d30fa9a66413e29290f69056683c8a490d5fbaf2a4d2)_.

body:

---|---
---
Dear Neighbors, Happy New Year to you and your family. I was contemplating many new years resolutions and thoughts the past few weeks, then I came across the Oregonian editorial a few days ago. It made me think, did I wake up in the "upside down" (look at me with my reference to "stranger things")? The editorial did a good job of laying out so many of the issues we have been working on since I was first elected in 2020. No political posturing, pushing agendas or even speaking out on federal issues I have no ability to control. I have always been focused on the issues; housing, economic development, education & child care and health care. These are not controversial but when you dig in, boy howdy are they.... Anyways, enjoy the read, and I put some comments in red parenthesis on my comments. Let's make 2026 great, **Senator Dick Anderson** Oregon State Senate District 5 _Contact: Sen.DickAnderson@oregonlegislature.gov | 503-986-1705_ _Visit:_[_www.oregonlegislature.gov/anderson_](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/http:%2F%2Fwww.oregonlegislature.gov%2Fanderson/1/0101019b9ebbb7e0-cd99c57f-06db-4813-a606-718513afebfe-000000/Sh7kX0tQOPzZjsIjA9fn861YOCurAThMXceIFt39Cjo=439) **[Editorial: Make 2026 the year of Oregon’s comeback](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Flinks-2.govdelivery.com%2FCL0%2Fhttps:%252F%252Fwww.msn.com%252Fen-us%252Fmoney%252Fmarkets%252Feditorial-make-2026-the-year-of-oregon-s-comeback%252Far-AA1Ty5Ye%253Focid=BingNewsVerp%2F1%2F0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000%2FR_RcxJaGg0acupIu-uamzCaaX9tO-tm8JKr1eFRq1FU=438/1/0101019b9ebbb7e0-cd99c57f-06db-4813-a606-718513afebfe-000000/syEWYDw4yCwDnU3c4bHJLTCR69VaP9qjep-80ZFUg4s=439 "https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.msn.com%2Fen-us%2Fmoney%2Fmarkets%2Feditorial-make-2026-the-year-of-oregon-s-comeback%2Far-AA1Ty5Ye%3Focid=BingNewsVerp/1/0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000/R_RcxJaGg0acupIu-uamzCaaX9tO-tm8JKr1eFRq1FU=438")
** _The Oregonian Editorial Board
_ It’s only through hindsight that you can recognize the point when you bottomed out and began a comeback. As we kick off the new year, it’s too soon to see in which direction Oregon is headed.
Will this be the year that enough elected officials, business executives, community leaders and voters work together to put Oregon on a path to recovery? Or will bickering – both across parties and within them – keep us laboring at cross purposes?
Even the most optimistic or oblivious of Oregonians should see the warning signs of what’s at stake.
Oregon has lost nearly 9,000 jobs in the past year – undermining not only those families’ economic stability but our income-tax dependent state’s as well. Iconic office towers in downtown Portland are selling for pennies on the dollar, part of a trend of [plummeting property value](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Flinks-2.govdelivery.com%2FCL0%2Fhttps:%252F%252Fwww.oregonlive.com%252Fbusiness%252F2025%252F12%252Fportland-office-sales-will-drive-millions-in-property-tax-losses-year-in-review.html%2F1%2F0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000%2FSJ3anV1nzFP08TN1o-IFGl3TcPRKiYJEVgFPzkgF0bY=438/1/0101019b9ebbb7e0-cd99c57f-06db-4813-a606-718513afebfe-000000/Ujn8gO2eB_cys6NeGQsdEHNyCSb4jxyERsyIztxr-Y0=439 "https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.oregonlive.com%2Fbusiness%2F2025%2F12%2Fportland-office-sales-will-drive-millions-in-property-tax-losses-year-in-review.html/1/0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000/SJ3anV1nzFP08TN1o-IFGl3TcPRKiYJEVgFPzkgF0bY=438") that is eroding revenue for local governments. Our dismal record of housing and caring for people in need faces new threats amid changing federal policies and declining financial assistance. Oregon’s educational system fails to help students master basic skills, even as the future grows increasingly complex and demanding. And years of little to no population growth reflect how greatly Oregon’s national reputation has tarnished.
These aren’t manufactured issues by Oregon haters to make the state look bad. They’re not scare tactics to bully elected leaders into succumbing to the whims of one special interest or another. These are structural threats that are crumbling the foundation for Oregon’s success and endangering the state’s ability to command its own agenda.
As we wrote last week, our leaders’ handling of turmoil in 2025 gave Oregonians reasons for both confidence and concern. There can’t be any confusion about which direction to take in 2026, however. They – and Oregonians as a whole – will need to make progress in these critical areas to ensure that we’ve turned the corner for good.
**Remake Oregon’s business climate as a place for investment and** **growth:** Private sector businesses, from corporate behemoths to small coffeeshops, drive our economy. They employ Oregonians whose income taxes power the state’s general fund; pay taxes and fees that directly support state spending, K-12 education and local governments; and deliver essential goods, services and amenities that Oregon communities need to thrive.
So, Oregon’s economic news of the past year – Great-Recession-level job losses, third highest unemployment rate in the country, [business closures](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Flinks-2.govdelivery.com%2FCL0%2Fhttps:%252F%252Ftualatinlife.com%252Fbusiness%252Fcampbells-soup-to-close-tualatin-pacific-foods-plant-in-phased-shutdown%252F%2F1%2F0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000%2FDiqdK6Z_yupwYGtBeq97NUggjY76C8jQIUyjdIc7pUY=438/1/0101019b9ebbb7e0-cd99c57f-06db-4813-a606-718513afebfe-000000/tAXuOyoZkBUZpr44eqBvcoekqPD59jurEm2szHGrYjg=439 "https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Ftualatinlife.com%2Fbusiness%2Fcampbells-soup-to-close-tualatin-pacific-foods-plant-in-phased-shutdown%2F/1/0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000/DiqdK6Z_yupwYGtBeq97NUggjY76C8jQIUyjdIc7pUY=438") and [out-of-state expansions](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Flinks-2.govdelivery.com%2FCL0%2Fhttps:%252F%252Fwww.hamptonlumber.com%252Fhampton-lumber-to-build-new-sawmill-in-south-carolina%252F%2F1%2F0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000%2F28RAFTGOb5k67glhPlSURxzbIg5wX7fCsdP2ww-W-QY=438/1/0101019b9ebbb7e0-cd99c57f-06db-4813-a606-718513afebfe-000000/paPjD-ZTO6Z14dfAfUTzf_Orc-iOS5ygnWhUZnoPDRM=439 "https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.hamptonlumber.com%2Fhampton-lumber-to-build-new-sawmill-in-south-carolina%2F/1/0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000/28RAFTGOb5k67glhPlSURxzbIg5wX7fCsdP2ww-W-QY=438") – should grab the attention of every elected leader in the state. Growing our economy, particularly as the federal government ratchets down funding, is the only way that Oregon will come up with the money it needs to pay for its many priorities.
There are plenty of places to improve. Oregon’s competitiveness has dropped sharply in recent years, as additional mandates, added taxes and lower affordability all make the state a riskier place to do business. Oregon was [ranked 21st just two years ago](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Flinks-2.govdelivery.com%2FCL0%2Fhttps:%252F%252Fwww.cnbc.com%252F2023%252F07%252F11%252Ftop-states-for-business-oregon.html%2F1%2F0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000%2FpRyJWYpA9H5LhukIv5wcCMfCPYifkEaxBjM3r5M3D3w=438/1/0101019b9ebbb7e0-cd99c57f-06db-4813-a606-718513afebfe-000000/fkD5NIqJX0WCfFUjF7xu0xRyzRV0PkXnmI3BF7jSSoE=439 "https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.cnbc.com%2F2023%2F07%2F11%2Ftop-states-for-business-oregon.html/1/0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000/pRyJWYpA9H5LhukIv5wcCMfCPYifkEaxBjM3r5M3D3w=438") in CNBC’s top states for business but [fell to 39th last year](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Flinks-2.govdelivery.com%2FCL0%2Fhttps:%252F%252Fwww.cnbc.com%252F2025%252F07%252F10%252Foregon-top-states-for-business-ranking.html%2F1%2F0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000%2FJu8kKL6wlhPcZD4uPnivQNopon2GmW6IWi7ZBI_gyrU=438/1/0101019b9ebbb7e0-cd99c57f-06db-4813-a606-718513afebfe-000000/oyu7Qifem1zu2QwxYDmvlwEJ_g3DG1bdIpsBXkXIFCU=439 "https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.cnbc.com%2F2025%2F07%2F10%2Foregon-top-states-for-business-ranking.html/1/0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000/Ju8kKL6wlhPcZD4uPnivQNopon2GmW6IWi7ZBI_gyrU=438"). In the categories of cost of doing business, cost of living and business friendliness, Oregon rated 43rd, 45th and 48th worst in the country, respectively.
Certainly, lowering or streamlining the state’s myriad taxes and reporting requirements could help. Businesses paid $3.4 billion more in state taxes in 2023 than just four years earlier due primarily to the new statewide corporate activity tax and paid leave payroll tax, [according to an EY study](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Flinks-2.govdelivery.com%2FCL0%2Fhttps:%252F%252Foregonbusinessindustry.com%252Fwp-content%252Fuploads%252FOregon-Business-Industry-FY24-FINAL.pdf%2F1%2F0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000%2FCE4ONMGykYsA46tDCWqZ9I4ieBLar2MYLxDvVHQyqrk=438/1/0101019b9ebbb7e0-cd99c57f-06db-4813-a606-718513afebfe-000000/Viop-kuocQ5boWX_vCmWsISOXLG09UZoPqBXl0V9qAw=439 "https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Foregonbusinessindustry.com%2Fwp-content%2Fuploads%2FOregon-Business-Industry-FY24-FINAL.pdf/1/0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000/CE4ONMGykYsA46tDCWqZ9I4ieBLar2MYLxDvVHQyqrk=438") commissioned by Oregon Business and Industry. The tax burden is even higher for businesses in the Portland area, where voters in recent years adopted a regional homeless services tax and a Portland clean energy tax.
But growing our economy must first start with a change in mindset among legislators and voters. Too often, they view businesses with hostility or ignore their warnings over consequences as irrelevant. They pass labor policies that are [more expansive](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Flinks-2.govdelivery.com%2FCL0%2Fhttps:%252F%252Fwww.oregonlive.com%252Fopinion%252F2025%252F01%252Feditorial-merry-christmas-labor-unions-love-gov-kotek.html%2F1%2F0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000%2Fcw_n7LMyJwAkpDZiVJuwh2Y7XPJYRJDTaRtVavEte68=438/1/0101019b9ebbb7e0-cd99c57f-06db-4813-a606-718513afebfe-000000/_gin-tDu61Fk7n-NgXjW_Z0bLi2Q6VNwKxNWrI2FSTU=439 "https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.oregonlive.com%2Fopinion%2F2025%2F01%2Feditorial-merry-christmas-labor-unions-love-gov-kotek.html/1/0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000/cw_n7LMyJwAkpDZiVJuwh2Y7XPJYRJDTaRtVavEte68=438") or generous than a[nywhere else in the country ](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Flinks-2.govdelivery.com%2FCL0%2Fhttps:%252F%252Fwww.oregonlive.com%252Fopinion%252F2025%252F06%252Feditorial-blinders-on-legislators-press-on-with-sb-916.html%2F1%2F0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000%2FsRosALLMbRWjCZKbgq-dfZCZ9BYNiCG6MY53SlFMhOw=438/1/0101019b9ebbb7e0-cd99c57f-06db-4813-a606-718513afebfe-000000/gYdIofWaBFIivgVvpb0lebXcdgX5-gIN2If3iUZ2yzM=439 "https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.oregonlive.com%2Fopinion%2F2025%2F06%2Feditorial-blinders-on-legislators-press-on-with-sb-916.html/1/0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000/sRosALLMbRWjCZKbgq-dfZCZ9BYNiCG6MY53SlFMhOw=438")while dismissing the increased costs to Oregon’s employers. The governor and state leaders cannot claim to be [open for business ](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Flinks-2.govdelivery.com%2FCL0%2Fhttps:%252F%252Fwww.opb.org%252Farticle%252F2025%252F12%252F02%252Foregon-governor-tina-kotek-ready-tackle-state-lousy-business-reputation%252F%2F1%2F0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000%2FPhCZauoiLJzg41e5loMTc1AbXC-2rv3ddua1ZKDp93w=438/1/0101019b9ebbb7e0-cd99c57f-06db-4813-a606-718513afebfe-000000/NFd1i3-oKgiVZQfTDR4aSyWaj2SFYGe7TwzDKQYhRls=439 "https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.opb.org%2Farticle%2F2025%2F12%2F02%2Foregon-governor-tina-kotek-ready-tackle-state-lousy-business-reputation%2F/1/0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000/PhCZauoiLJzg41e5loMTc1AbXC-2rv3ddua1ZKDp93w=438")when they adopt punitive requirements that [other states reject](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Flinks-2.govdelivery.com%2FCL0%2Fhttps:%252F%252Fwww.gov.ca.gov%252Fwp-content%252Fuploads%252F2024%252F09%252FSB-984-Veto-Message.pdf%2F1%2F0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000%2FE0AYgFa1KCezN5D5WBM8tRNL6FmC2cx2p79mvpnpM2M=438/1/0101019b9ebbb7e0-cd99c57f-06db-4813-a606-718513afebfe-000000/44dd2MZYm0MIkO7GSuNxIZsGlJyqszsVc6wDhqD-P2A=439 "https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.gov.ca.gov%2Fwp-content%2Fuploads%2F2024%2F09%2FSB-984-Veto-Message.pdf/1/0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000/E0AYgFa1KCezN5D5WBM8tRNL6FmC2cx2p79mvpnpM2M=438").
And they fail to recognize how Oregon sometimes gets in its own way. A statewide cap on rent increases, which has already been ratcheted down, is just one more factor discouraging investors from backing desperately needed housing development in Oregon. Oregon needs more land that can quickly be converted to industrial use, but land-use law makes it easy for opponents to block such progress through the courts. While businesses will certainly act to protect their own interests, policymakers should realize that keeping them around is in Oregon’s interests as well.
**Halt our K-12 educational system freefall:** Oregon embraces the bare minimum when it comes to educating students. The state has one of the shortest school years in the country, lets students skip the state’s annual standardized exam for any reason they like and has yet to reinstate a graduation requirement that was first waived for the pandemic.
Meanwhile, student test scores show that a majority of students [aren’t meeting proficiency standards](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Flinks-2.govdelivery.com%2FCL0%2Fhttps:%252F%252Fwww.oregonlive.com%252Feducation%252F2025%252F10%252Fminuscule-test-score-gains-signal-oregon-faces-years-of-digging-out-from-its-post-pandemic-academic-hole.html%2F1%2F0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000%2FBD_k2CCP7aNElbESlmvkv1uri2sAHfElBHFfWmCSdMw=438/1/0101019b9ebbb7e0-cd99c57f-06db-4813-a606-718513afebfe-000000/wp2pBCOls3cAR8_3qIZMGgqNnOGN1InvOXgNLWTibVo=439 "https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.oregonlive.com%2Feducation%2F2025%2F10%2Fminuscule-test-score-gains-signal-oregon-faces-years-of-digging-out-from-its-post-pandemic-academic-hole.html/1/0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000/BD_k2CCP7aNElbESlmvkv1uri2sAHfElBHFfWmCSdMw=438") in math or reading and are still underachieving pre-pandemic levels. With districts poised to make [significant cuts in the coming year ](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Flinks-2.govdelivery.com%2FCL0%2Fhttps:%252F%252Fwww.oregonlive.com%252Feducation%252F2025%252F11%252Foregon-school-leaders-are-sounding-the-alarm-about-mid-year-budget-cuts-heres-what-they-want-for-a-fix.html%2F1%2F0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000%2FRRBk4HFGRAquVOZgTf7LtykWjAxA5Nu5rYg77OXmXyo=438/1/0101019b9ebbb7e0-cd99c57f-06db-4813-a606-718513afebfe-000000/brTmL4dKWJLeY8fw5kPwwUxkBeR8uN8Q4MlC9UzUFGY=439 "https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.oregonlive.com%2Feducation%2F2025%2F11%2Foregon-school-leaders-are-sounding-the-alarm-about-mid-year-budget-cuts-heres-what-they-want-for-a-fix.html/1/0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000/RRBk4HFGRAquVOZgTf7LtykWjAxA5Nu5rYg77OXmXyo=438")due to insufficient funding, students will likely be receiving less help, not more. (We have to go back to higher standards for our students. Lowering standards will continue to lower the output)
While Gov. Tina Kotek has led significant investments in improving literacy for young students and championed an “accountability” bill for stronger oversight of poor-performing districts, that’s not nearly enough to address our dysfunctional system.
Among the needs: the state must have an honest conversation about education funding. The state’s 40-plus-year-old funding formula fails to capture today’s needs and may be [shorting higher-poverty districts ](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Flinks-2.govdelivery.com%2FCL0%2Fhttps:%252F%252Fwww.oregonlive.com%252Feducation%252F2025%252F05%252Foregons-school-funding-formula-undercounts-poverty-denying-some-districts-millions-lawmakers-are-poised-to-approve-it-anyway.html%2F1%2F0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000%2FtidsbDBVRjwAxNm_FPB_fnto-2hDEs15CYMqoaCfl4M=438/1/0101019b9ebbb7e0-cd99c57f-06db-4813-a606-718513afebfe-000000/OiuXFdFQGkEtsw4VWAFWFp1_V0_tP4vFdVO5iPc1uQI=439 "https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.oregonlive.com%2Feducation%2F2025%2F05%2Foregons-school-funding-formula-undercounts-poverty-denying-some-districts-millions-lawmakers-are-poised-to-approve-it-anyway.html/1/0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000/tidsbDBVRjwAxNm_FPB_fnto-2hDEs15CYMqoaCfl4M=438")of some of the money they are owed. Legislators [hound school districts to pay teachers more](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Flinks-2.govdelivery.com%2FCL0%2Fhttps:%252F%252Fwww.oregonlive.com%252Fopinion%252F2023%252F11%252Feditorial-pps-teachers-union-must-cut-a-deal.html%2F1%2F0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000%2FFW0_tRb6r2THjtMt2FbXNAwS2cO3YLrc7dJQlKQQw1w=438/1/0101019b9ebbb7e0-cd99c57f-06db-4813-a606-718513afebfe-000000/uzlZ-p19PTkv1MzCn3NDnC1WPj99N53udR3mfBxpG8Y=439 "https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.oregonlive.com%2Fopinion%2F2023%2F11%2Feditorial-pps-teachers-union-must-cut-a-deal.html/1/0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000/FW0_tRb6r2THjtMt2FbXNAwS2cO3YLrc7dJQlKQQw1w=438") while sidestepping their own failure to provide enough money. Unfunded mandates and overwhelming pension obligations are starving instructional budgets. At the same time, districts and their boards must also be transparent with spending on any [non-core responsibilities](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Flinks-2.govdelivery.com%2FCL0%2Fhttps:%252F%252Fwww.oregonlive.com%252Fopinion%252F2025%252F08%252Feditorial-ppss-fast-tracked-vote-dodges-critical-questions.html%2F1%2F0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000%2FRGqnODMMMIotIM2TDsAei7XWTKxpWaTPzhW7ixSgALE=438/1/0101019b9ebbb7e0-cd99c57f-06db-4813-a606-718513afebfe-000000/CouulccyK8dHMxH9aufKB_R6jOeHF6kNS5D3wCfoBzA=439 "https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.oregonlive.com%2Fopinion%2F2025%2F08%2Feditorial-ppss-fast-tracked-vote-dodges-critical-questions.html/1/0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000/RGqnODMMMIotIM2TDsAei7XWTKxpWaTPzhW7ixSgALE=438") or contracts.
The state must also insist that students get at least the minimum number of instructional hours, rather than allow districts to close budget deficits by cutting school days as [Reynolds School District is planning](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Flinks-2.govdelivery.com%2FCL0%2Fhttps:%252F%252Fwww.oregonlive.com%252Feducation%252F2025%252F10%252Fbudget-deal-would-save-reynolds-teacher-jobs-but-shorten-school-year.html%2F1%2F0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000%2F0yP_lstWBJx05E_IB-S5YeiYO_gRTRcp-z6zDZTa5oA=438/1/0101019b9ebbb7e0-cd99c57f-06db-4813-a606-718513afebfe-000000/BbyUfI0lS8hM1evooceNnQ6lZk1KrRJdo-8WF-Ofbgg=439 "https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.oregonlive.com%2Feducation%2F2025%2F10%2Fbudget-deal-would-save-reynolds-teacher-jobs-but-shorten-school-year.html/1/0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000/0yP_lstWBJx05E_IB-S5YeiYO_gRTRcp-z6zDZTa5oA=438"). School district budgets cannot be balanced by reducing an already short school year. Education leaders should also explore whether district consolidations could help preserve opportunities for students.
A strong public educational system isn’t just about fulfilling the most basic obligation to Oregon’s children; it’s also vital to attracting and retaining families and businesses who want a state that invests in its future.
**Spend the public’s money responsibly:** Want proof that Oregonians are fed up with the cost of living in Oregon? Consider the enormous popularity of a [recent petition to refer $4.8 billion](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Flinks-2.govdelivery.com%2FCL0%2Fhttps:%252F%252Fwww.oregonlive.com%252Fpolitics%252F2025%252F12%252Foregonians-wont-see-gas-tax-transportation-fee-hikes-in-january-as-opponents-secure-enough-signatures-to-send-issue-to-ballot.html%2F1%2F0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000%2Fjb350OColOj-oNpuGN0QolKgtofo0xx1byOCPk3hoRY=438/1/0101019b9ebbb7e0-cd99c57f-06db-4813-a606-718513afebfe-000000/WEDaZpPaljLXv-QMyzpMoqyVOFGqCNB_hR1um2aZ1bM=439 "https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.oregonlive.com%2Fpolitics%2F2025%2F12%2Foregonians-wont-see-gas-tax-transportation-fee-hikes-in-january-as-opponents-secure-enough-signatures-to-send-issue-to-ballot.html/1/0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000/jb350OColOj-oNpuGN0QolKgtofo0xx1byOCPk3hoRY=438") of new transportation taxes and fees to the November ballot. In a few weeks, organizers collected a quarter of a million signatures – 8% of the total number of registered voters statewide – easily qualifying for the ballot. Legislators will need to address in the short legislative session how to fill a massive hole in the state transportation budget, not to mention local agencies, which had been counting on a share of the new revenue. (This is a result of not working together in a real bipartisan way, one party rule will drive the other party to react in this way every time)
The transportation tax referendum is one obvious example of Oregonians’ frustration with ever-increasing taxes, but Oregon faces a financial reckoning on multiple levels. Federal tax changes will lead to less Oregon tax revenue, due to the state’s automatic adoption of the federal tax code, while President Donald Trump’s budget bill will lead to less funding for Medicaid and other Oregon programs. Not only are Trump’s tariffs continuing to drive up costs for consumers and businesses, but retaliatory tariffs are hitting Oregon’s farmers, manufacturers and other exporters. And ongoing layoffs and slower job growth loom large over Oregon’s finances. (There is no evidence that tariffs are driving up costs, and inflation has flattened since he took office)
With such uncertainty, Oregon leaders must make the difficult decision of choosing which among its many priorities to protect and deciding how to fund them. And Oregon’s elected officials must work to earn back Oregonians’ trust in their spending decisions after passing such uniquely bad legislation as last year’s bill [providing unemployment pay for striking workers](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Flinks-2.govdelivery.com%2FCL0%2Fhttps:%252F%252Fwww.oregonlive.com%252Fopinion%252F2025%252F06%252Feditorial-blinders-on-legislators-press-on-with-sb-916.html%2F2%2F0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000%2F0FW_em9n_auxTHKEoAdSNhwzZN2KkKO8s2qyPj5bEL0=438/1/0101019b9ebbb7e0-cd99c57f-06db-4813-a606-718513afebfe-000000/O_0cQZ4tTtO6t0AzZF-eYavCI6nxoPdWRAPLzHC-g2c=439 "https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.oregonlive.com%2Fopinion%2F2025%2F06%2Feditorial-blinders-on-legislators-press-on-with-sb-916.html/2/0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000/0FW_em9n_auxTHKEoAdSNhwzZN2KkKO8s2qyPj5bEL0=438"), which hits school districts and other public agencies particularly hard. As the transportation referendum shows, even if Oregonians support a core service such as road maintenance, they will not easily accept big tax and fee increases amid an affordability crisis.
The same need for financial stewardship applies to local governments as well. As business license fees and downtown property tax revenue decline, Portland and Multnomah County are facing tightening budgets and difficult choices. Meanwhile, specialty taxes funding clean energy projects and preschool have brought in hundreds of millions of dollars more than expected. Elected leaders of both jurisdictions should ask voters to give them additional flexibility in how to use those surplus dollars to help cover essential services.
**Revive the Portland core both economically and civically:** Downtown Portland commercial office buildings have [a 36% vacancy rate](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Flinks-2.govdelivery.com%2FCL0%2Fhttps:%252F%252Fmktgdocs.cbre.com%252F2299%252F3acb3e6f-25b5-45df-b44c-4e2ee42353a2-648150182%252FCBRE_Portland_Office_Figures_R.pdf%2F1%2F0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000%2FIuDx-7ERZYY1zTwcW6muG3nZTmphUMeXkhxh7AbcHOY=438/1/0101019b9ebbb7e0-cd99c57f-06db-4813-a606-718513afebfe-000000/4qU-O73LMHz_tNYVevGmylsVOGYZ0HCTBKRLIhW3FAY=439 "https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fmktgdocs.cbre.com%2F2299%2F3acb3e6f-25b5-45df-b44c-4e2ee42353a2-648150182%2FCBRE_Portland_Office_Figures_R.pdf/1/0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000/IuDx-7ERZYY1zTwcW6muG3nZTmphUMeXkhxh7AbcHOY=438") while longtime retailers, including Nordstrom Rack, are calling it quits. Even [as other cities bounce back](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Flinks-2.govdelivery.com%2FCL0%2Fhttps:%252F%252Fwww.oregonlive.com%252Fbusiness%252F2025%252F03%252F5-years-later-portland-lags-other-cities-as-it-nurses-pandemic-era-wounds.html%2F1%2F0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000%2FlVzSeBSRa0cEkkLxfQZ7WgO2-j7qgYJPTe72Ugenaik=438/1/0101019b9ebbb7e0-cd99c57f-06db-4813-a606-718513afebfe-000000/dQ7SzussZXHAoPVB12izv2mWYn3etK-WAYGK_DBPHJs=439 "https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.oregonlive.com%2Fbusiness%2F2025%2F03%2F5-years-later-portland-lags-other-cities-as-it-nurses-pandemic-era-wounds.html/1/0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000/lVzSeBSRa0cEkkLxfQZ7WgO2-j7qgYJPTe72Ugenaik=438") and are showing job gains since the pandemic, Portland’s downtown still bears its scars, as well as those of the 2020 protests-turned-riots and the shift to a work-from-home culture.
Public safety initiatives have helped improve the look and feel of downtown, and Portland Mayor Keith Wilson’s emphasis on reducing unsanctioned camping and open drug use should remain a key part of rebuilding downtown as a destination for Oregonians and visitors. His decision to call back roughly 700 managers and supervisors to full time, in-person work was also a smart move that increases foot traffic and better serves the public. The mayor should work with the business community to explore how to incentivize more workers to return to the office and what the city can do to keep businesses operating downtown.
Reviving Portland isn’t just about buildings, however. Portland has a number of promising initiatives that the city should support or help fast track, whether it’s through financial, logistical or political means. The renovation of the Portland Art Museum, which was funded almost entirely by private donations, should help further a conversation about how to re-establish the city as a top cultural and entertainment destination in the Northwest. Efforts to redevelop Albina, Portland’s historically Black district, offer a singular opportunity for the city to address past wrongs and support economic revitalization. And the purchase of the Portland Trail Blazers should lead to a clear commitment from the city, region and state to keep the team in Portland, even if that means helping finance a renovated arena.
All these initiatives are reminders of the many strengths Portland has and can build on for the future. The city and its residents should lean into them.
**Get people housed:** Kotek declared homelessness [a state of emergency in January 2023](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Flinks-2.govdelivery.com%2FCL0%2Fhttps:%252F%252Fwww.oregon.gov%252Fohcs%252Fhomelessness-response%252Fpages%252Fdefault.aspx%2F1%2F0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000%2FqeSPLTaLQbm7pX3aanuy5ydy02gtTJ2u2UGmNsAm1tI=438/1/0101019b9ebbb7e0-cd99c57f-06db-4813-a606-718513afebfe-000000/xALhDUbotELQ7lEmY4McoL65ge82gI5AahLOu3GWZHo=439 "https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.oregon.gov%2Fohcs%2Fhomelessness-response%2Fpages%2Fdefault.aspx/1/0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000/qeSPLTaLQbm7pX3aanuy5ydy02gtTJ2u2UGmNsAm1tI=438"). The city of Portland declared a [housing state of emergency in 2015](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Flinks-2.govdelivery.com%2FCL0%2Fhttps:%252F%252Fwww.oregonlive.com%252Fportland%252F2015%252F10%252Fportland_approves_housing_emer.html%2F1%2F0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000%2FYdVG0WrnwmLyoToOfOA0z8f5cjjbFNDOSGeBq084uco=438/1/0101019b9ebbb7e0-cd99c57f-06db-4813-a606-718513afebfe-000000/or__foyL7TiZCEjHF4azYnJV2kWovff5A0F3AKXucuA=439 "https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.oregonlive.com%2Fportland%2F2015%2F10%2Fportland_approves_housing_emer.html/1/0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000/YdVG0WrnwmLyoToOfOA0z8f5cjjbFNDOSGeBq084uco=438"). And yet, despite spending billions of dollars in recent years into housing developments, rental assistance, social services and shelters, the housing and homelessness crisis hasn’t lessened. (Homelessness has become a culture issue not just a "problem" this is why it is so difficult to solve as people are choosing it as a lifestyle. We must tackle the underlying issue of drugs and mental health, or this will never be "solved")
Even when there’s progress in some areas, new problems keep cropping up. In Portland, about [1,900 taxpayer-funded affordable housing ](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Flinks-2.govdelivery.com%2FCL0%2Fhttps:%252F%252Fwww.oregonlive.com%252Fbusiness%252F2025%252F12%252Fnearly-1900-affordable-portland-apartments-sit-empty-while-thousands-need-homes.html%2F1%2F0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000%2FoMaWM5FoADTjAIL41vBwylkK06e2F_Mb6FZpEqUWZeQ=438/1/0101019b9ebbb7e0-cd99c57f-06db-4813-a606-718513afebfe-000000/gBfIRFhkV0ZUbVdjCLNxPcqYiFQgn41hY3wnseUZHOo=439 "https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.oregonlive.com%2Fbusiness%2F2025%2F12%2Fnearly-1900-affordable-portland-apartments-sit-empty-while-thousands-need-homes.html/1/0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000/oMaWM5FoADTjAIL41vBwylkK06e2F_Mb6FZpEqUWZeQ=438")units sit vacant due to difficult application processes and rents that aren’t much lower than market rate. Affordable housing providers are [on the ropes, financially](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Flinks-2.govdelivery.com%2FCL0%2Fhttps:%252F%252Fwww.oregonlive.com%252Fbusiness%252F2025%252F12%252Fportland-affordable-housing-is-in-financial-collapse-can-it-be-salvaged.html%2F1%2F0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000%2FIPCVX82iB_UxC4_OZvRSXYbL0DxqITFozVtqD7axmGE=438/1/0101019b9ebbb7e0-cd99c57f-06db-4813-a606-718513afebfe-000000/q1X_rNNtlX-jLnVGz63D__EvqyX4_QJ95F-7U7DWqTc=439 "https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.oregonlive.com%2Fbusiness%2F2025%2F12%2Fportland-affordable-housing-is-in-financial-collapse-can-it-be-salvaged.html/1/0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000/IPCVX82iB_UxC4_OZvRSXYbL0DxqITFozVtqD7axmGE=438"). And as important as Wilson’s emergency shelter plan has been, it is only one part of the full spectrum of housing needed to move people from the streets to stability.
In a true emergency, policymakers don’t erect barriers to meeting the need. State and local officials must adopt that same urgent, focused approach by removing the financial and logistical obstacles blocking communities from adding housing or shelter. For instance, legislators should make explicitly clear that affordable housing developments are exempt from paying higher “prevailing wage” requirements, despite such rulings from Labor Commissioner Christina Stephenson for projects including a commercial space, as [Oregon Journalism Project](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Flinks-2.govdelivery.com%2FCL0%2Fhttps:%252F%252Fwww.wweek.com%252Fnews%252F2025%252F04%252F02%252Fare-oregons-top-democrats-more-interested-in-housing-the-poor-or-helping-their-campaign-donors%252F%2F1%2F0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000%2Fd8cATUil9j_PyVtGA3mAXVVDlT6KhSbXhUvR7_XcnfA=438/1/0101019b9ebbb7e0-cd99c57f-06db-4813-a606-718513afebfe-000000/iqDCSmDQewwleXv6PRG6WBtAGaHB-s21dKW6pgr8uOM=439 "https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.wweek.com%2Fnews%2F2025%2F04%2F02%2Fare-oregons-top-democrats-more-interested-in-housing-the-poor-or-helping-their-campaign-donors%2F/1/0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000/d8cATUil9j_PyVtGA3mAXVVDlT6KhSbXhUvR7_XcnfA=438") has documented. (I will be introducing a bill to do just that in the short session in February, if it is swept under the rug or not even heard by the majority party they are not serious about solving housing.)
Similarly, legislators should gear up for a review of Oregon’s land use laws to examine whether the nearly 53-year-old statute provides enough flexibility to accommodate a state population that has almost doubled since then.
**Demand competence in government:** The need for competent management and better execution of programs applies to all levels of government. The state’s bungled rollout of [Medicaid dollars for rent assistance](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Flinks-2.govdelivery.com%2FCL0%2Fhttps:%252F%252Fwww.oregonlive.com%252Fhealth%252F2025%252F08%252Foregon-scrambles-to-address-delays-for-medicaid-funded-rent-assistance.html%2F1%2F0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000%2FvhoSOoGtthHO4RJ_Zv5jUMPFor7gWHY2tiMWigAom14=438/1/0101019b9ebbb7e0-cd99c57f-06db-4813-a606-718513afebfe-000000/QTIKq0_thvK9v031Ft1qQgZyuJm-xBBNC3cfwHtgenk=439 "https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.oregonlive.com%2Fhealth%2F2025%2F08%2Foregon-scrambles-to-address-delays-for-medicaid-funded-rent-assistance.html/1/0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000/vhoSOoGtthHO4RJ_Zv5jUMPFor7gWHY2tiMWigAom14=438") and Multnomah County’s [little-used deflection center](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Flinks-2.govdelivery.com%2FCL0%2Fhttps:%252F%252Fwww.oregonlive.com%252Fpolitics%252F2025%252F11%252Fwith-annual-data-in-pressure-is-on-multnomah-county-to-increase-use-of-expensive-new-deflection-center.html%2F1%2F0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000%2Fom3rE8vRIXhu-AC96ArBuvLvdgSivrVPyowMPPo_6n0=438/1/0101019b9ebbb7e0-cd99c57f-06db-4813-a606-718513afebfe-000000/c7oUHK6VHmyoVh6lrtmFoBtA3JLTKVeWWB3dekjWvIY=439 "https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.oregonlive.com%2Fpolitics%2F2025%2F11%2Fwith-annual-data-in-pressure-is-on-multnomah-county-to-increase-use-of-expensive-new-deflection-center.html/1/0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000/om3rE8vRIXhu-AC96ArBuvLvdgSivrVPyowMPPo_6n0=438") for drug users are among the many examples where outcomes failed to meet the goals.
But it’s especially relevant to the city of Portland, which completed a first – and rough – year under a new form of city government.
While Wilson focused primarily on his goal to open emergency overnight beds and begin enforcement of the camping ban, the 12 city councilors [didn’t coalesce around many priorities](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Flinks-2.govdelivery.com%2FCL0%2Fhttps:%252F%252Fwww.oregonlive.com%252Fpolitics%252F2025%252F09%252Fportland-city-stall-councilors-struggle-to-find-their-governance-groove.html%2F1%2F0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000%2F2RnYKrJNmwO4mTzWUb6pMTCHDU7uj4FdUzO5l88iI4s=438/1/0101019b9ebbb7e0-cd99c57f-06db-4813-a606-718513afebfe-000000/Z5mmsq3uKmhbMxuav1xZ2bpEOORsHgbsc_4pmUX396o=439 "https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.oregonlive.com%2Fpolitics%2F2025%2F09%2Fportland-city-stall-councilors-struggle-to-find-their-governance-groove.html/1/0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000/2RnYKrJNmwO4mTzWUb6pMTCHDU7uj4FdUzO5l88iI4s=438"), bickered about minutiae and failed to land a signature achievement. Although the Council certainly deserves more time than a year to prove this new format is an improvement, councilors [must show they are capable](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Flinks-2.govdelivery.com%2FCL0%2Fhttps:%252F%252Fwww.oregonlive.com%252Fopinion%252F2025%252F09%252Feditorial-pull-it-together-portland-city-council.html%2F1%2F0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000%2FleG3QnEsOUUl0PplUtYiP5KEbCp--Kaz6Z3IvkQJew8=438/1/0101019b9ebbb7e0-cd99c57f-06db-4813-a606-718513afebfe-000000/0MV2KnV4WIdpSAgzJaBG-28rpDeTJvzM-L5L41FlTWk=439 "https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.oregonlive.com%2Fopinion%2F2025%2F09%2Feditorial-pull-it-together-portland-city-council.html/1/0101019b9049b8e6-4146b41d-8567-4e6b-a92d-c0739966dba2-000000/leG3QnEsOUUl0PplUtYiP5KEbCp--Kaz6Z3IvkQJew8=438") of solving Portland’s biggest problems, especially as the city faces another year of potentially devastating budget cuts.
Oregonians also bear responsibility for ensuring an effective, transparent and accountable government. With so many key offices on the ballot this year, Oregonians should carefully consider candidates’ records and demonstrated competence when they vote.
**Keep Oregon in charge of its agenda:** Trump’s attempt to send troops to Portland was the biggest surprise to hit Oregon last year, but it certainly wasn’t the only one. Chances are 2026 will deliver plenty of new, unforeseeable challenges. That’s all the more reason for Oregon’s leaders and residents to continue to show the restraint, prudence and strategic action that they demonstrated throughout the federal troop saga. Oregon can stay in control of its priorities, but must keep its cool to do so.
Progress comes with ups and downs. But by the end of the year, Oregon’s leaders must be able to show that they’ve led the state to higher ground.

clean_body: | | | "View Online" ---|--- Dear Neighbors, Happy New Year to you and your family. I was contemplating many new years resolutions and thoughts the past few weeks, then I came across the Oregonian editorial a few days ago. It made me think, did I wake up in the "upside down" (look at me with my reference to "stranger things")? The editorial did a good job of laying out so many of the issues we have been working on since I was first elected in 2020. No political posturing, pushing agendas or even speaking out on federal issues I have no ability to control. I have always been focused on the issues; housing, economic development, education & child care and health care. These are not controversial but when you dig in, boy howdy are they.... Anyways, enjoy the read, and I put some comments in red parenthesis on my comments. Let's make 2026 great, Senator Dick Anderson Oregon State Senate District 5 Contact: Sen.DickAnderson@oregonlegislature.gov | 503-986-1705 Visit: "" The Oregonian Editorial Board It’s only through hindsight that you can recognize the point when you bottomed out and began a comeback. As we kick off the new year, it’s too soon to see in which direction Oregon is headed. Will this be the year that enough elected officials, business executives, community leaders and voters work together to put Oregon on a path to recovery? Or will bickering – both across parties and within them – keep us laboring at cross purposes? Even the most optimistic or oblivious of Oregonians should see the warning signs of what’s at stake. Oregon has lost nearly 9,000 jobs in the past year – undermining not only those families’ economic stability but our income-tax dependent state’s as well. Iconic office towers in downtown Portland are selling for pennies on the dollar, part of a trend of "" that is eroding revenue for local governments. Our dismal record of housing and caring for people in need faces new threats amid changing federal policies and declining financial assistance. Oregon’s educational system fails to help students master basic skills, even as the future grows increasingly complex and demanding. And years of little to no population growth reflect how greatly Oregon’s national reputation has tarnished. These aren’t manufactured issues by Oregon haters to make the state look bad. They’re not scare tactics to bully elected leaders into succumbing to the whims of one special interest or another. These are structural threats that are crumbling the foundation for Oregon’s success and endangering the state’s ability to command its own agenda. As we wrote last week, our leaders’ handling of turmoil in 2025 gave Oregonians reasons for both confidence and concern. There can’t be any confusion about which direction to take in 2026, however. They – and Oregonians as a whole – will need to make progress in these critical areas to ensure that we’ve turned the corner for good. Remake Oregon’s business climate as a place for investment and growth: Private sector businesses, from corporate behemoths to small coffeeshops, drive our economy. They employ Oregonians whose income taxes power the state’s general fund; pay taxes and fees that directly support state spending, K-12 education and local governments; and deliver essential goods, services and amenities that Oregon communities need to thrive. So, Oregon’s economic news of the past year – Great-Recession-level job losses, third highest unemployment rate in the country, "" and "" – should grab the attention of every elected leader in the state. Growing our economy, particularly as the federal government ratchets down funding, is the only way that Oregon will come up with the money it needs to pay for its many priorities. There are plenty of places to improve. Oregon’s competitiveness has dropped sharply in recent years, as additional mandates, added taxes and lower affordability all make the state a riskier place to do business. Oregon was "" in CNBC’s top states for business but "". In the categories of cost of doing business, cost of living and business friendliness, Oregon rated 43rd, 45th and 48th worst in the country, respectively. Certainly, lowering or streamlining the state’s myriad taxes and reporting requirements could help. Businesses paid $3.4 billion more in state taxes in 2023 than just four years earlier due primarily to the new statewide corporate activity tax and paid leave payroll tax, "" commissioned by Oregon Business and Industry. The tax burden is even higher for businesses in the Portland area, where voters in recent years adopted a regional homeless services tax and a Portland clean energy tax. But growing our economy must first start with a change in mindset among legislators and voters. Too often, they view businesses with hostility or ignore their warnings over consequences as irrelevant. They pass labor policies that are "" or generous than a ""while dismissing the increased costs to Oregon’s employers. The governor and state leaders cannot claim to be ""when they adopt punitive requirements that "". And they fail to recognize how Oregon sometimes gets in its own way. A statewide cap on rent increases, which has already been ratcheted down, is just one more factor discouraging investors from backing desperately needed housing development in Oregon. Oregon needs more land that can quickly be converted to industrial use, but land-use law makes it easy for opponents to block such progress through the courts. While businesses will certainly act to protect their own interests, policymakers should realize that keeping them around is in Oregon’s interests as well. Halt our K-12 educational system freefall: Oregon embraces the bare minimum when it comes to educating students. The state has one of the shortest school years in the country, lets students skip the state’s annual standardized exam for any reason they like and has yet to reinstate a graduation requirement that was first waived for the pandemic. Meanwhile, student test scores show that a majority of students "" in math or reading and are still underachieving pre-pandemic levels. With districts poised to make ""due to insufficient funding, students will likely be receiving less help, not more. (We have to go back to higher standards for our students. Lowering standards will continue to lower the output) While Gov. Tina Kotek has led significant investments in improving literacy for young students and championed an “accountability” bill for stronger oversight of poor-performing districts, that’s not nearly enough to address our dysfunctional system. Among the needs: the state must have an honest conversation about education funding. The state’s 40-plus-year-old funding formula fails to capture today’s needs and may be ""of some of the money they are owed. Legislators "" while sidestepping their own failure to provide enough money. Unfunded mandates and overwhelming pension obligations are starving instructional budgets. At the same time, districts and their boards must also be transparent with spending on any "" or contracts. The state must also insist that students get at least the minimum number of instructional hours, rather than allow districts to close budget deficits by cutting school days as "". School district budgets cannot be balanced by reducing an already short school year. Education leaders should also explore whether district consolidations could help preserve opportunities for students. A strong public educational system isn’t just about fulfilling the most basic obligation to Oregon’s children; it’s also vital to attracting and retaining families and businesses who want a state that invests in its future. Spend the public’s money responsibly: Want proof that Oregonians are fed up with the cost of living in Oregon? Consider the enormous popularity of a "" of new transportation taxes and fees to the November ballot. In a few weeks, organizers collected a quarter of a million signatures – 8% of the total number of registered voters statewide – easily qualifying for the ballot. Legislators will need to address in the short legislative session how to fill a massive hole in the state transportation budget, not to mention local agencies, which had been counting on a share of the new revenue. (This is a result of not working together in a real bipartisan way, one party rule will drive the other party to react in this way every time) The transportation tax referendum is one obvious example of Oregonians’ frustration with ever-increasing taxes, but Oregon faces a financial reckoning on multiple levels. Federal tax changes will lead to less Oregon tax revenue, due to the state’s automatic adoption of the federal tax code, while President Donald Trump’s budget bill will lead to less funding for Medicaid and other Oregon programs. Not only are Trump’s tariffs continuing to drive up costs for consumers and businesses, but retaliatory tariffs are hitting Oregon’s farmers, manufacturers and other exporters. And ongoing layoffs and slower job growth loom large over Oregon’s finances. (There is no evidence that tariffs are driving up costs, and inflation has flattened since he took office) With such uncertainty, Oregon leaders must make the difficult decision of choosing which among its many priorities to protect and deciding how to fund them. And Oregon’s elected officials must work to earn back Oregonians’ trust in their spending decisions after passing such uniquely bad legislation as last year’s bill "", which hits school districts and other public agencies particularly hard. As the transportation referendum shows, even if Oregonians support a core service such as road maintenance, they will not easily accept big tax and fee increases amid an affordability crisis. The same need for financial stewardship applies to local governments as well. As business license fees and downtown property tax revenue decline, Portland and Multnomah County are facing tightening budgets and difficult choices. Meanwhile, specialty taxes funding clean energy projects and preschool have brought in hundreds of millions of dollars more than expected. Elected leaders of both jurisdictions should ask voters to give them additional flexibility in how to use those surplus dollars to help cover essential services. Revive the Portland core both economically and civically: Downtown Portland commercial office buildings have "" while longtime retailers, including Nordstrom Rack, are calling it quits. Even "" and are showing job gains since the pandemic, Portland’s downtown still bears its scars, as well as those of the 2020 protests-turned-riots and the shift to a work-from-home culture. Public safety initiatives have helped improve the look and feel of downtown, and Portland Mayor Keith Wilson’s emphasis on reducing unsanctioned camping and open drug use should remain a key part of rebuilding downtown as a destination for Oregonians and visitors. His decision to call back roughly 700 managers and supervisors to full time, in-person work was also a smart move that increases foot traffic and better serves the public. The mayor should work with the business community to explore how to incentivize more workers to return to the office and what the city can do to keep businesses operating downtown. Reviving Portland isn’t just about buildings, however. Portland has a number of promising initiatives that the city should support or help fast track, whether it’s through financial, logistical or political means. The renovation of the Portland Art Museum, which was funded almost entirely by private donations, should help further a conversation about how to re-establish the city as a top cultural and entertainment destination in the Northwest. Efforts to redevelop Albina, Portland’s historically Black district, offer a singular opportunity for the city to address past wrongs and support economic revitalization. And the purchase of the Portland Trail Blazers should lead to a clear commitment from the city, region and state to keep the team in Portland, even if that means helping finance a renovated arena. All these initiatives are reminders of the many strengths Portland has and can build on for the future. The city and its residents should lean into them. Get people housed: Kotek declared homelessness "". The city of Portland declared a "". And yet, despite spending billions of dollars in recent years into housing developments, rental assistance, social services and shelters, the housing and homelessness crisis hasn’t lessened. (Homelessness has become a culture issue not just a "problem" this is why it is so difficult to solve as people are choosing it as a lifestyle. We must tackle the underlying issue of drugs and mental health, or this will never be "solved") Even when there’s progress in some areas, new problems keep cropping up. In Portland, about ""units sit vacant due to difficult application processes and rents that aren’t much lower than market rate. Affordable housing providers are "". And as important as Wilson’s emergency shelter plan has been, it is only one part of the full spectrum of housing needed to move people from the streets to stability. In a true emergency, policymakers don’t erect barriers to meeting the need. State and local officials must adopt that same urgent, focused approach by removing the financial and logistical obstacles blocking communities from adding housing or shelter. For instance, legislators should make explicitly clear that affordable housing developments are exempt from paying higher “prevailing wage” requirements, despite such rulings from Labor Commissioner Christina Stephenson for projects including a commercial space, as "" has documented. (I will be introducing a bill to do just that in the short session in February, if it is swept under the rug or not even heard by the majority party they are not serious about solving housing.) Similarly, legislators should gear up for a review of Oregon’s land use laws to examine whether the nearly 53-year-old statute provides enough flexibility to accommodate a state population that has almost doubled since then. Demand competence in government: The need for competent management and better execution of programs applies to all levels of government. The state’s bungled rollout of "" and Multnomah County’s "" for drug users are among the many examples where outcomes failed to meet the goals. But it’s especially relevant to the city of Portland, which completed a first – and rough – year under a new form of city government. While Wilson focused primarily on his goal to open emergency overnight beds and begin enforcement of the camping ban, the 12 city councilors "", bickered about minutiae and failed to land a signature achievement. Although the Council certainly deserves more time than a year to prove this new format is an improvement, councilors "" of solving Portland’s biggest problems, especially as the city faces another year of potentially devastating budget cuts. Oregonians also bear responsibility for ensuring an effective, transparent and accountable government. With so many key offices on the ballot this year, Oregonians should carefully consider candidates’ records and demonstrated competence when they vote. Keep Oregon in charge of its agenda: Trump’s attempt to send troops to Portland was the biggest surprise to hit Oregon last year, but it certainly wasn’t the only one. Chances are 2026 will deliver plenty of new, unforeseeable challenges. That’s all the more reason for Oregon’s leaders and residents to continue to show the restraint, prudence and strategic action that they demonstrated throughout the federal troop saga. Oregon can stay in control of its priorities, but must keep its cool to do so. Progress comes with ups and downs. But by the end of the year, Oregon’s leaders must be able to show that they’ve led the state to higher ground. My rank and retirement are things that I earned through my service and sacrifice for this country. Generations of servicemembers have done the same. Pete Hegseth wants to send a message to every single one that he will come after them if they say something he doesn’t like.

Friend — Yesterday, in Minneapolis, ICE murdered an innocent woman named Renee Nicole Good in cold blood.
Many of us saw the video. What happened was clear as day. The ICE officer who fired the fatal shots had no reason to even draw his weapon. **It was not self-defense.**
But that’s not stopping the sick tyrants who currently inhabit the White House to spin a web of lies.
Within minutes of the shooting, DHS Secretary Kristi Noem rushed to say that Renee, an artist, poet, and mother of three, was engaged in “an act of domestic terrorism” at the time she was killed. That's an absurd and downright evil lie.
DHS followed up with an official statement claiming that Renee was “attempting to run over our law enforcement officers in an attempt to kill them”, something that is completely unbelievable to anyone who watches the video.

We cannot let that happen. She needs thousands of grassroots patriots--just like you--to rally to her side RIGHT NOW if we're going to take back Arizona. Karrin doesn't have a billion-dollar machine behind her. What she has is the MAGA movement. The people. The patriots. You. Will you step up today to help her fight back? # Trump bans Wall Street home buying spree
President Donald Trump announced Wednesday he's[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/f250d3a4-94f1-4979-83bc-6471dff3abb7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[taking immediate steps](https://substack.com/redirect/f250d3a4-94f1-4979-83bc-6471dff3abb7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to ban large institutional investors from purchasing single-family homes, blaming corporate buyers for driving up prices and making the American Dream unaffordable for many, especially younger buyers.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f250d3a4-94f1-4979-83bc-6471dff3abb7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Blames Biden inflation** for eroding homeownership while pledging congressional action to codify the ban, stating "people live in homes, not corporations"
* **Triggers stock drops** as shares of Invitation Homes plunged 6%, Blackstone over 5%, and Apollo Global Management similarly declined
* **Cites soaring prices** with median existing single-family home at $426,800 in Q3 2025 amid 6.19% mortgage rates
* **GOP senator prefers** supply-focused bipartisan "ROAD to Housing" bill over ban, while Trump plans more proposals at Davos speech

# Mamdani backs appointee amid white supremacy uproar
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani is defending his newly appointed tenants' rights chief, Cea Weaver, against fierce backlash over her resurfaced old social media posts that **[labeled homeownership a"weapon of white supremacy"](https://substack.com/redirect/a7aa8ba1-e94e-409c-a4ac-2d5e547701c9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and called for treating private property as a collective good.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2bc0d70b-edfa-4c7f-a506-af6b7f8c6d6a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Weaver expresses regret** over past statements, calling some "regretful" and emphasizing her current focus on safe, affordable housing for all renters and owners alike.
* **Prior posts were known** to administration before appointment, with a spokesperson confirming officials were aware of the deleted social media content.
* **Critics pile on** including former Mayor Eric Adams, who slammed the remarks as showing "extreme privilege and total detachment from reality," plus condemnations from Justice Department officials and The Washington Post editorial board.
* **Contrasts recent resignation** of another Mamdani appointee over antisemitic posts, highlighting ongoing scrutiny of the new mayor's early personnel choices in his tenant-protection push.

* * *
* * *
# Trump bans defense dividends for late and over budget eauipment
President Donald Trump issued an executive order Wednesday **[blocking major defense contractors](https://substack.com/redirect/cdc9388c-a0ce-45f0-a6c2-c30365e4b1aa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** from paying dividends or repurchasing shares until they accelerate weapons production and deliver superior equipment on time and on budget, sending shares tumbling amid criticism of industry priorities.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/cdc9388c-a0ce-45f0-a6c2-c30365e4b1aa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Executive order details** restrict payouts effective immediately, prioritizing warfighter needs over investor returns in a rare challenge to Wall Street practices.
* **Targeted underperformers face** identification by Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth within 30 days, with opportunities to submit remediation plans or risk government enforcement.
* **Stock market reacts sharply** as Lockheed Martin dropped 4.8%, Northrop Grumman 5.5%, and General Dynamics 3.6% after Trump's social media posts.
* **Raytheon singled out** for slowest response to military needs, producing key systems like Patriot missiles heavily used in Ukraine and Tomahawk missiles.

* * *
* * *
# Dallas poised for NYC exodus "avalanche"
Dallas Mayor Eric Johnson predicted Wednesday that an **["avalanche" of New York City financial firms](https://substack.com/redirect/23c45bee-9d8a-4c60-9c90-752fe5b87b30?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** will flee to his city, citing new Mayor Zohran Mamdani's socialist policies like higher business taxes and city-owned grocery stores as driving the exodus.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/23c45bee-9d8a-4c60-9c90-752fe5b87b30?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Socialist Policies Criticized** : Mamdani's agenda includes fare-free buses and increased taxes on wealthy individuals and job creators, labeled "un-American" by Johnson.
* **Dallas Welcomes Businesses** : Johnson emphasized Dallas doesn't "demonize successful businesses" and positions it as "America's Sanctuary City from Socialism."
* **Texas Tax Advantages** : Relocating firms benefit from no state income tax, reduced property taxes for seven years, and lower overall cost of living.
* **Major Firms Expanding** : Examples include JPMorgan Chase employing more in Texas than New York and Goldman Sachs building a large Dallas campus.

* * *
* * *
# Alaska Airlines bets big on Boeing
Alaska Airlines announced its **[largest-ever aircraft order Wednesday,](https://substack.com/redirect/ab436d11-5669-400f-be7d-a897e77ef5da?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** committing to 105 Boeing 737 Max 10 jets and five 787-10 Dreamliners in a major vote of confidence for the planemaker exactly two years after a terrifying midflight door plug blowout on one of its 737 Max 9s.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ab436d11-5669-400f-be7d-a897e77ef5da?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Largest Order Ever** : Deal includes 53 firm 737 Max 10s plus 52 converted options, with rights for 35 more.
* **Fleet Growth Strategy** : Roughly half the new jets replace older aircraft, while the rest support expansion to 550 planes by 2035.
* **International Expansion Push** : Order follows Hawaiian Airlines acquisition, enabling new nonstop routes to destinations like Italy and South Korea.
* **Delivery Timeline Set** : 737 Max 10 deliveries are to begin in 2027 after expected FAA certification this year.

name: Gabby Giffords
subject: January 8, 2011
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY SCHIFF FOR SENATE
body:
[ https://act.adamschiff.com/go/1014?c0=q12026_abs_em_giffords.ISRIoU&refcode=AU_ABS_FR_TAN_GEN_AC90_20260108_PM1_V1_S1&t=1003&akid=9391%2E5257348%2Ez836K- ]Gabby Giffords

Hello Derek,

It’s Gabby Giffords. On January 8, 2011 — 15 years ago today — my life
forever changed when a gunman attempted to assassinate me while I was
hosting a constituent event in Tucson, Arizona.

Six innocent people were killed that day: Christina-Taylor, Dorothy, Judge
John Roll, Phyllis, Dorwan, and Gabe. I’ll never forget their names.
Twelve others were injured.

That shooting turned my life upside down. The bullet damaged the left side
of my brain, where language is processed, leading to a condition called
aphasia. While speaking is still difficult for me, I have never given up
on my recovery journey, even on the most difficult days.

[ https://act.adamschiff.com/go/1014?c0=q12026_abs_em_giffords.ISRIoU&refcode=AU_ABS_FR_TAN_GEN_AC90_20260108_PM1_V1_S1&t=1004&akid=9391%2E5257348%2Ez836K- ]15 years ago, Gabby Giffords was attacked by a gunman at an event in
Tucson

The anniversary of this shooting is a painful one, but it also serves as a
reminder of the way that we can come together in the wake of tragedy. I
relearned how to walk and talk, and became a stronger Gabby — a healing
journey that I continue on to this day.

Two years after I was shot, another life-altering shooting occurred — this
time at Sandy Hook Elementary in Newtown, where 20 children and six adults
were murdered.

I knew in that moment I had to do something, so Mark Kelly and I founded
GIFFORDS with the mission to end gun violence and create a safer future
for our nation’s communities.

[ https://act.adamschiff.com/go/1014?c0=q12026_abs_em_giffords.ISRIoU&refcode=AU_ABS_FR_TAN_GEN_AC90_20260108_PM1_V1_S1&t=1005&akid=9391%2E5257348%2Ez836K- ]Gabby Giffords and Mark Kelly

When we founded GIFFORDS, many people warned us that it would be political
poison to stand up against the gun lobby. They had millions of dollars at
their disposal, and would use every cent to drown us out.

But the progress we’ve made is undeniable. We’ve beaten back the NRA and
made gun safety a winning issue, thanks to supporters like you.

Now, we face an inflection point. President Trump’s administration is
working to roll back our progress on gun safety — putting all of their
weight towards flooding our streets with more guns and helping their gun
manufacturing buddies profit.

I know we have what it takes to end the gun violence epidemic in our
country. But I cannot do it alone.

[ https://act.adamschiff.com/go/1014?c0=q12026_abs_em_giffords.ISRIoU&refcode=AU_ABS_FR_TAN_GEN_AC90_20260108_PM1_V1_S1&email=&t=1006&akid=9391%2E5257348%2Ez836K- ]So I am humbly asking: Can you please split a donation between GIFFORDS
PAC and Senator Adam Schiff before the clock strikes midnight?

If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your split
donation will go through immediately:

[ https://act.adamschiff.com/go/1015?c0=q12026_abs_em_giffords.6bLc90&refcode=AU_ABS_FR_TAN_GEN_AC90_20260108_PM1_V1_S1&t=1007&akid=9391%2E5257348%2Ez836K- ]EXPRESS DONATE $10

[ https://act.adamschiff.com/go/1016?c0=q12026_abs_em_giffords.65NT-z&refcode=AU_ABS_FR_TAN_GEN_AC90_20260108_PM1_V1_S1&t=1008&akid=9391%2E5257348%2Ez836K- ]EXPRESS DONATE $25

[ https://act.adamschiff.com/go/1017?c0=q12026_abs_em_giffords.fK1CI-&refcode=AU_ABS_FR_TAN_GEN_AC90_20260108_PM1_V1_S1&t=1009&akid=9391%2E5257348%2Ez836K- ]EXPRESS DONATE $50

[ https://act.adamschiff.com/go/1018?c0=q12026_abs_em_giffords.JgufuC&refcode=AU_ABS_FR_TAN_GEN_AC90_20260108_PM1_V1_S1&t=1010&akid=9391%2E5257348%2Ez836K- ]EXPRESS DONATE $100

[ https://act.adamschiff.com/go/1019?c0=q12026_abs_em_giffords.uxoTaA&refcode=AU_ABS_FR_TAN_GEN_AC90_20260108_PM1_V1_S1&t=1011&akid=9391%2E5257348%2Ez836K- ]EXPRESS DONATE $250

[ https://act.adamschiff.com/go/2142?c0=q12026_abs_em_giffords.ZYi-uX&refcode=AU_ABS_FR_TAN_GEN_AC90_20260108_PM1_V1_S1&t=1012&akid=9391%2E5257348%2Ez836K- ]ANOTHER AMOUNT

That day in Tucson captured national attention — a sitting Congresswoman
shot in the head. But the truth is that today, being shot isn’t rare. Gun
violence is a national crisis and now the leading cause of death for
American kids and teens.

Make no mistake: the fight isn’t over yet, and the headwinds we face are
stiff. But if we all keep working together, I know that someday, there
will be a future where we no longer live under the constant threat of gun
violence.

clean_body: [ - ]Gabby Giffords Hello Derek, It’s Gabby Giffords. On January 8, 2011 — 15 years ago today — my life forever changed when a gunman attempted to assassinate me while I was hosting a constituent event in Tucson, Arizona. Six innocent people were killed that day: Christina-Taylor, Dorothy, Judge John Roll, Phyllis, Dorwan, and Gabe. I’ll never forget their names. Twelve others were injured. That shooting turned my life upside down. The bullet damaged the left side of my brain, where language is processed, leading to a condition called aphasia. While speaking is still difficult for me, I have never given up on my recovery journey, even on the most difficult days. [ - ]15 years ago, Gabby Giffords was attacked by a gunman at an event in Tucson The anniversary of this shooting is a painful one, but it also serves as a reminder of the way that we can come together in the wake of tragedy. I relearned how to walk and talk, and became a stronger Gabby — a healing journey that I continue on to this day. Two years after I was shot, another life-altering shooting occurred — this time at Sandy Hook Elementary in Newtown, where 20 children and six adults were murdered. I knew in that moment I had to do something, so Mark Kelly and I founded GIFFORDS with the mission to end gun violence and create a safer future for our nation’s communities. [ - ]Gabby Giffords and Mark Kelly When we founded GIFFORDS, many people warned us that it would be political poison to stand up against the gun lobby. They had millions of dollars at their disposal, and would use every cent to drown us out. But the progress we’ve made is undeniable. We’ve beaten back the NRA and made gun safety a winning issue, thanks to supporters like you. Now, we face an inflection point. President Trump’s administration is working to roll back our progress on gun safety — putting all of their weight towards flooding our streets with more guns and helping their gun manufacturing buddies profit. I know we have what it takes to end the gun violence epidemic in our country. But I cannot do it alone. [ - ]So I am humbly asking: Can you please split a donation between GIFFORDS PAC and Senator Adam Schiff before the clock strikes midnight? If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation will go through immediately: [ - ]EXPRESS DONATE $10 [ - ]EXPRESS DONATE $25 [ - ]EXPRESS DONATE $50 [ - ]EXPRESS DONATE $100 [ - ]EXPRESS DONATE $250 [ - ]ANOTHER AMOUNT That day in Tucson captured national attention — a sitting Congresswoman shot in the head. But the truth is that today, being shot isn’t rare. Gun violence is a national crisis and now the leading cause of death for American kids and teens. Make no mistake: the fight isn’t over yet, and the headwinds we face are stiff. But if we all keep working together, I know that someday, there will be a future where we no longer live under the constant threat of gun violence. | | **Thanks to the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, Everett and Mukilteo will get the resources they need to improve the safety of streets and roads to save lives.** Last month, the Department of Transportation announced nearly $1 billion in Safe Streets and Roads for All (SS4A) grant funding for projects aimed at improving road safety for all users, including pedestrians and cyclists. The SS4A program, which invests $5 billion over five years in regional, local and Tribal initiatives to prevent roadway deaths and serious injuries, was established under the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law. **Two projects in Northwest Washington were awarded grants totaling $1.5 million in this round of grant announcements:** $1.2 million for the City of Everett and $300,000 for the City of Mukilteo. Washington was awarded a total of more than $9.9 million for 15 projects. This is on top of the funding I secured from the Department of Transportation at the end of December:
* **$1,238,680 for the Nooksack Indian Tribe** to remove a culvert in Jones Creek under a BNSF Railway line in Acme
* **$1,876,265 for Lummi Indian Business Council** to build a new bus maintenance facility
* **$8,862,951 for Whatcom Transportation Authority** to replace eight 2011 diesel buses with eight low or no-emission buses
* **$9,644,865 for Whatcom Transportation Authority** to purchase 11 low or no-emission buses to replace three diesel buses and eight hybrid buses
* **$2,000,000 for the City of Burlington** to identify which of the city’s 16 at-grade rail crossings is most suitable for grade separation to improve safety and reduce traffic congestion
* **$80,000 for the City of Ferndale’s** Road Safety Improvement Plan
* **$95,000 for Samish Indian Nation’s** Transportation Safety Action Plan
* **$100,000 for the City of Sedro-Woolley’s** SS4A Action Plan
* **$18,090,000 for the City of Everett** to eliminate two at-grade railroad crossings that pose significant risks to public safety through the construction of an overpass and a new integrated roundabout near the Smith Island railroad terminal in Everett
* **$400,000 for the City of Everett** to develop a supplemental Speed Management Plan
