I am unbelievably angry about what happened to Renee Nicole Good--the woman who was murdered in Minneapolis yesterday by an ICE agent. No matter where you stand on immigration, this was unjustifiable. She did not deserve to die--and the videos and witness testimony make that aggressively clear.
I grew up in a law enforcement household. In moments like this, I usually call my dad. He's a 34-year veteran of the FBI, and I get his take--because he's been trained to be in the kinds of high-pressure situations like this one.
I'm going to keep most of that conversation private, because he asked me to. But there's one thing I want to share: my dad will often say, "Imagine it was me out there--thinking my life or the lives of other officers were in danger." And I get that. Every cop walks into a shift knowing it might be their last.
But I pushed back, like I did yesterday. I told him: What if it was me in that car? What if it was me protesting ICE? What if it was me standing up for what I believe in? Do I deserve to die?
Because Renee didn't. Not by any reasonable standard. I guarantee you that, based on everything I've seen.
She leaves behind a six-year-old son--the same age as my own kid. Her husband died a few years ago. That little boy is alone now. His life will never be the same. Thank God his grandfather is still alive to raise him.
This is heartbreaking. And it never should have happened.
ICE should never have been there in the first place--terrorizing immigrant communities, conducting raids without warrants, snatching people up based on the color of their skin, not their immigration status. Not whether they committed an actual crime. Just rounding people up. It's happening in Chicago. It's happening in Minneapolis. It's happening all over. And it is wrong.
It's also not popular.
Donald Trump is wildly unpopular on immigration. And that matters--because the arrogance you see from Trump, J.D. Vance, Stephen Miller, and the rest of these MAGA types is staggering.
They truly believe they'll never be held accountable for what they're doing. And that is obscene. I'll echo what Mayor Frey said yesterday after the shooting:
ICE--get the fuck out of our cities. Nobody wants you here.
Now, let's address what actually happened.
Renee Nicole Good was sitting in her car, parked, and was waving ICE cars past her. When she realized what was happening, she tried to leave. She was scared--as anyone would be when masked, armed men with their hands on their weapons are reaching into your vehicle--and she wasn't trying to hit anybody, as the Trump administration has claimed.
And now you've got people online saying, "Well, if she'd just followed commands, she'd still be alive."
But eyewitnesses on the ground say ICE agents--many of whom are untrained, incompetent, and outright disgraces to law enforcement--were shouting conflicting orders. One agent told her to go. Another told her to stop.
This is what happens when you hire unqualified people and give them guns.
These agents aren't ready. They're not trained. They have no idea what they're doing.
When you're in the FBI, like my father was, or you become a police officer, you go through serious, intensive training. That doesn't mean every cop is great--but most of them know the basics: de-escalation, clear commands, accountability. These guys don't.
They've built a private army for Donald Trump. That's what ICE is now--a rogue militia for targeting anyone who steps out of line. And every ICE agent who's signed up for this knows they can act with impunity. We've seen the horror stories across the country. We've seen people die.
And they know they won't be held accountable.
They know Trump's DOJ won't touch them.
They know even if someone tries to hold them accountable later, Trump will just pardon them.
That's the real reason Trump pardoned the January 6th rioters. He doesn't give a shit about them. It was a message: If you do my dirty work, I've got your back. No matter what.
And now we're dealing with a runaway boulder barreling down a hill.
It's terrifying.
The immigrant communities being terrorized by ICE don't deserve this.
Yes--secure the border.
Yes--remove people who commit violent crimes.
But fix the damn immigration system so people who are already here--where the only difference between them and me is a fucking piece of paper--can be citizens. Can contribute. Can pay taxes. Can live like human beings. Can support their families and their communities.
And stop chasing Stephen Miller's wet dream where everyone in America has to be white.
And by the way--if you think Stephen Miller is going to stop with undocumented Hispanic immigrants, think again.
They want to come for people born here.
They want to purge anyone who doesn't fit their twisted fantasy of racial purity.
I'm Irish and Italian. I doubt I even make the cut in Stephen Miller's America.
One final thought:
With all the outrage porn out there--the manufactured bullshit people try to rile you up over--this shooting is something actually worth getting mad about.
Hold on to that outrage.
Organize in your community.
Protect your people.
Demand your reps in Congress do something.
Demand justice--however much of it we can get with Trump and Pam Bondi running the DOJ.
And come November? The reckoning is coming for these guys.

subject: Today is a very important day
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Jon Ossoff for SenateThis email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail
body:
#

[
---
Hello Peter, It’s Gabby Giffords. On January 8, 2011 — 15 years ago today — my life forever changed when a gunman attempted to assassinate me while I was hosting a constituent event in Tucson, Arizona. Six innocent people were killed that day: Christina-Taylor, Dorothy, Judge John Roll, Phyllis, Dorwan, and Gabe. I’ll never forget their names. Twelve others were injured. That shooting turned my life upside down. The bullet damaged the left side of my brain, where language is processed, leading to a condition called aphasia. While speaking is still difficult for me, I have never given up on my recovery journey, even on the most difficult days. [](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-jan26-giffords.8AO0CR&refcode=em260108-2-f&t=2&akid=1404%2E5691347%2EX5LZud) The anniversary of this shooting is a painful one, but it also serves as a reminder of the way that we can come together in the wake of tragedy. I relearned how to walk and talk, and became a stronger Gabby — a healing journey that I continue on to this day. Two years after I was shot, another life-altering shooting occurred — this time at Sandy Hook Elementary in Newtown, where 20 children and six adults were murdered. I knew in that moment I had to do something, so Mark Kelly and I founded GIFFORDS with the mission to end gun violence and create a safer future for our nation’s communities. [](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-jan26-giffords.8AO0CR&refcode=em260108-2-f&t=3&akid=1404%2E5691347%2EX5LZud) When we founded GIFFORDS, many people warned us that it would be political poison to stand up against the gun lobby. They had millions of dollars at their disposal, and would use every cent to drown us out. But the progress we’ve made is undeniable. We’ve beaten back the NRA and made gun safety a winning issue, thanks to supporters like you. Now, we face an inflection point. President Trump’s administration is working to roll back our progress on gun safety — putting all of their weight towards flooding our streets with more guns and helping their gun manufacturing buddies profit. I know we have what it takes to end the gun violence epidemic in our country. But I cannot do it alone. **[So I am humbly asking: Can you please split a donation between GIFFORDS PAC and Jon Ossoff before the clock strikes midnight?](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-jan26-giffords.8AO0CR&refcode=em260108-2-f&t=4&akid=1404%2E5691347%2EX5LZud)** _If you 've stored your info with ActBlue, we'll process your split contribution to Jon Ossoff and GIFFORDS PAC instantly:_ | | **[CONTRIBUTE $10](https://act.electjon.com/go/1525?c0=ossoff-em-jan26-giffords.MdPPvR&refcode=em260108-2-f&t=23&akid=1404%2E5691347%2EX5LZud)**
---
**** | **[CONTRIBUTE $25](https://act.electjon.com/go/1526?c0=ossoff-em-jan26-giffords.vdZJVw&refcode=em260108-2-f&t=24&akid=1404%2E5691347%2EX5LZud)**
---
****
| | **[CONTRIBUTE $50](https://act.electjon.com/go/1520?c0=ossoff-em-jan26-giffords.PsEADu&refcode=em260108-2-f&t=25&akid=1404%2E5691347%2EX5LZud)**
---
**** | **[CONTRIBUTE $100](https://act.electjon.com/go/1521?c0=ossoff-em-jan26-giffords.z26cPX&refcode=em260108-2-f&t=26&akid=1404%2E5691347%2EX5LZud)**
---
****
| | **[CONTRIBUTE $250](https://act.electjon.com/go/1522?c0=ossoff-em-jan26-giffords.K_caox&refcode=em260108-2-f&t=27&akid=1404%2E5691347%2EX5LZud)**
---
**** | **[Another Amount](https://act.electjon.com/go/34?c0=ossoff-em-jan26-giffords.Wme4xU&refcode=em260108-2-f&t=28&akid=1404%2E5691347%2EX5LZud)**
---
****
That day in Tucson captured national attention — a sitting Congresswoman shot in the head. But the truth is that today, being shot isn’t rare. Gun violence is a national crisis and now the leading cause of death for American kids and teens. Make no mistake: the fight isn’t over yet, and the headwinds we face are stiff. But if we all keep working together, I know that someday, there will be a future where we no longer live under the constant threat of gun violence. With courage, Gabby Giffords **[DONATE](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-jan26-giffords.8AO0CR&refcode=em260108-2-f&t=29&akid=1404%2E5691347%2EX5LZud)**

body:
Since Gabby was shot, and over the last few years especially, political violence has gotten out of control. But every person has a choice to make:
#

Folks,
15 years ago, while I was training for a shuttle mission, I got the phone call that Gabby was shot.
It was a punch in the gut like nothing I’ve ever felt before.
She survived, but six were killed and another twelve wounded. Our lives changed forever.
Since that day, and over the last few years especially, political violence has only gotten worse. It’s hard to know exactly what to do to stop it. But each of us has a choice:
Am I going to try to make things better, or worse?
For my part, the answer is easy. I am going to continue to try to bring people together instead of apart. That doesn’t mean I won’t disagree, and it certainly doesn’t mean I won’t fight for what I believe in.
We have to, for the sake of our kids and our grandkids.
Gabby’s example of courage, kindness, and hope in spite of everything that's been thrown at her keeps me going every day. And if you’re ever feeling like you don’t know how, believe me: Listen to her.
She’s pretty smart.
Thank you,
Mark

name: Saikat Chakrabarti
subject: I’m not running to climb the ladder of a broken system, I’m running to shake it’s very foundation
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY SAIKAT FOR CONGRESS
body:
We need to perform major surgery on our democracy to save it

| | | | | |
---
| | | | | | Friends –
Last night at the Working Families Party Congressional District 11 forum, I told the packed room something I deeply believe: we're living in unprecedented times.
AI, climate change, an authoritarian regime that just murdered a woman in Minneapolis.
If I told you 10 years ago we'd be sitting here today in this reality, you wouldn't have believed me.
But here we are.
In a moment, [**I’m going to ask you to chip in to our campaign**](https://saikat.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=6ed3ace2702e5b912b1693cee&id=aaf0b8512f&e=bf17056ae8), but first, let me explain why I’m running for office in the first place.
The only way we defeat MAGA and tackle these existential challenges is to do politics differently than we have for generations. We need to deliver a fundamentally better life for all. And to do that, we need to perform major surgery on the entire system.
That means taking on not just MAGA Republicans, but corporate money and a failed Democratic establishment. We need to completely change the direction and leadership of the Democratic Party.
I know this sounds ambitious. But I'm not the only one running to do it. **This is a change moment.** Candidates all over the country are challenging the establishment right now. Zohran just won.
And I’ve been building towards this moment since 2016, when I was the Director of Organizing Technology for Bernie. And in 2018, when I started Justice Democrats and recruited AOC to defeat the third most powerful Democrat in the country. When we created the Green New Deal that led to the largest investment in climate in US history.
**Last night made something clear to me: there's a real difference in this race.**
When asked if Israel is committing genocide in Gaza, I said yes. One of my opponents wouldn't.
When asked about Democratic leadership, I said what needed to be said: they've completely failed us. We're in an authoritarian coup, and our leaders are folding instead of fighting. We need legislators who see their job as organizers and fighters, not just policymakers.
I’m not running to climb the ladder of a broken system or build a career in politics, I’m running to deliver real change for working people.
Our campaign started with just a few of us. Now, we've knocked over 100,000 doors. We expected 100 people at our office opening—500 came. Our rally drew 800. Our town halls have been standing room only.
And the turnout isn’t _for_ me. People are coming because they're sick of the broken status quo. They want leadership that reimagines a society that works for working people and makes it real.
Throughout history, San Francisco has been home to movements that fix what the nation gets wrong. When the country wouldn't move, San Francisco pushed.
Our country needs San Francisco to push again.
So coming out of this forum, with momentum at our back, let’s keep pushing together.
[**Donate $1, $5, or whatever you can afford. We're running this campaign on small donations, not corporate money, and every dollar builds it from the ground up and sends a signal to the establishment.**](https://saikat.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=6ed3ace2702e5b912b1693cee&id=39a1909562&e=bf17056ae8)
---
| [DONATE »](https://saikat.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=6ed3ace2702e5b912b1693cee&id=d650ec7abf&e=bf17056ae8)
---
| | We have a once-in-a-generation opportunity to change what's possible. Let's build this movement together.
San Francisco can lead America out of the darkness once again.
In solidarity,Saikat
P.S. If you want to see the full forum, [**you can watch it here**](https://saikat.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=6ed3ace2702e5b912b1693cee&id=bb14f9248a&e=bf17056ae8).
---
|
---

He’s running for Congress to build a San Francisco that works for everyone—teachers, immigrants, service workers, and everyone else who makes this city the best in the world.
If you believe San Franciscans deserve affordable housing, universal healthcare, climate resilience, and public power: [volunteer](https://saikat.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=6ed3ace2702e5b912b1693cee&id=d2737a0424&e=bf17056ae8) with us and learn more about our campaign on our [website](https://saikat.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=6ed3ace2702e5b912b1693cee&id=6bb64a722c&e=bf17056ae8).
